area: Phase machine: phases, postures/run-states, transitions, entry/exit criteria, and "one pass" loop boundaries (project-manager skill)
overview: The project-manager skill drives a project through a fixed 9-phase pipeline (intake -> research -> design -> plan -> implement -> review -> cr -> confirming -> done) that is orthogonal to a 4-value scheduling "posture"/run-state (working/monitoring/needs_you/done). `state.phase` is the WHAT of work; `state.run.posture` is the scheduling stance that governs whether the session may yield. The authority for legal transitions and entry/crash-recovery order is references/state-machine.md; SKILL.md restates the same skeleton and adds the durable-checkpoint "one pass" boundary machinery, hook semantics, and stop triggers. A Rust harness must own two coupled state variables (phase + posture), a strict transition validator (many transitions are illegal, notably cr->done), and a per-unit checkpoint gate that defines where one loop pass ends.

elements.name: Phase: intake
elements.detail: First phase on a new/cold project. Confirms goal, package scope, communication destinations, and external-action approvals (state-machine.md:46-47). Outputs brief.md, config.json, approvals (SKILL.md:216). MUST complete before package + capability detection (SKILL.md:62; state-machine.md:45-47 step 6). Success transition -> research; 'stay for user clarification' otherwise (state-machine.md:118).
elements.porting_note: Enum variant Phase::Intake. Gate: package/CLI detection and toolchain population must not run until intake is marked complete. On brand-new project (state.toolchain==null and no brief) the harness routes here first.

elements.name: Phase: research
elements.detail: Output research/*.md (SKILL.md:217). Success -> design; 'stay while topics remain' (state-machine.md:119). Playbook references/phases/research.md.
elements.porting_note: Phase::Research. Advancement predicate: no research topics remain outstanding. Also the ONLY target of the done->research and confirming->[B] re-entry transitions.

elements.name: Phase: design
elements.detail: Output design.md (SKILL.md:218). Success -> plan; 'stay on an ambiguity stop' (state-machine.md:120). Playbook references/phases/design.md.
elements.porting_note: Phase::Design. Blocking is via open_stops (ambiguity), not a distinct phase; posture goes needs_you while the design ambiguity stop is open, phase stays design.

elements.name: Phase: plan
elements.detail: Output plan.md (SKILL.md:219). Success -> implement; 'stay while the plan is incomplete' (state-machine.md:121). Playbook references/phases/plan.md.
elements.porting_note: Phase::Plan. Plan produces slices + task cursors consumed by implement. Note reverse edge: implement->plan when no plan/cursor exists (recovery).

elements.name: Phase: implement
elements.detail: Output code and task digests (SKILL.md:220). Success -> review AT A SLICE BOUNDARY; 'stay while tasks remain'; -> plan if no plan/cursor exists (state-machine.md:122). Coordinator NEVER edits impl files; all changes dispatched through pm-worker.sh (SKILL.md:129-132).
elements.porting_note: Phase::Implement. Transition to review is keyed on 'slice boundary' (a slice's tasks are all done), not per-task. Keep a task_cursors[] concept; a cursor with no completion digest reconciles to a stop rather than re-dispatch (state-machine.md:150-151). Add recovery edge implement->plan.

elements.name: Phase: review
elements.detail: Output verification evidence (SKILL.md:221). Success -> cr; 'stay while fixing'; STOP (not a transition) when review_state.attempts >= stuck_threshold (state-machine.md:123; SKILL.md:363-364). Playbook references/phases/review.md.
elements.porting_note: Phase::Review. Hitting stuck_threshold does NOT change phase; it raises a stop (posture->needs_you) while phase stays review. Track review_state (see review_state element).

elements.name: Phase: cr
elements.detail: Output draft CR/PR records (SKILL.md:222). Success -> implement WHEN ANOTHER SLICE REMAINS; 'stay while CRs are open'; -> confirming ONLY when the plan is exhausted AND every CR is terminal (state-machine.md:124). cr->done is explicitly forbidden (state-machine.md:128).
elements.porting_note: Phase::Cr. This is the loop-back hub: cr->implement cycles per remaining slice. Guard confirming entry with (plan_exhausted && all_crs_terminal). Explicitly reject cr->done in the validator.

elements.name: Phase: confirming
elements.detail: Output explicit project decision (SKILL.md:223). Transitions (state-machine.md:125): -> done ONLY after explicit [A]; -> research on [B]; invariant-repair -> cr | implement | plan; stay on [C] or no reply. Requires user confirmation stop (SKILL.md:366).
elements.porting_note: Phase::Confirming. Model the user decision as an enum: A=accept->done, B=new-direction->research, C=not-yet->stay, plus an invariant-repair escape hatch that can jump back to cr/implement/plan. Posture is needs_you (confirmation stop) until a reply arrives.

elements.name: Phase: done
elements.detail: 'inline idle' — no local work (SKILL.md:224). Transitions: none; -> research ONLY for a new user ask (state-machine.md:126). done is idle: work:false, no routine status posts, no new external action; persist run.posture:done to turn off the harness; heartbeat may keep polling already-tracked threads until user runs cancel handle (SKILL.md:459-461).
elements.porting_note: Phase::Done. Couple with Posture::Done. In done, due-track `work` is forced false. Only a fresh user ask reopens (->research).

elements.name: Posture/run-state: working
elements.detail: A local action can run now. Do ONE meaningful unit, close its durable checkpoint before starting the next unit, renew the lease, recompute due tracks, reload the active playbook after any phase change, save run as working with the next local action as its wake condition, and keep going IN THE SAME ENTRY. The Stop hook rejects any attempt to yield here (SKILL.md:169-174). 'Working always loops' (SKILL.md:187).
elements.porting_note: Posture::Working. This is the non-yielding state: the daemon must not release the coordinator lease or end the pass while working. It is the ONLY posture that continues within the same entry; every checkpoint keeps run=working until the final posture mutation (see checkpoint gate).

elements.name: Posture/run-state: monitoring
elements.detail: No local action can run because something is in flight: an analyzer, a CI run, a CR/PR, or an expert reply. Record what owns the next update and when to check it, set run to monitoring, and let the heartbeat come back later instead of busy-waiting (SKILL.md:176-178). Default blocking worker NEVER produces this posture; sole exception is an opt-in detached async worker polled via due_async_workers (SKILL.md:180-183).
elements.porting_note: Posture::Monitoring. Requires (owner, next_poll_epoch). Releases the lease and yields to the heartbeat. A running async worker is a valid monitoring owner just like an open CR/CI run (state-machine.md:145-148).

elements.name: Posture/run-state: needs_you
elements.detail: A specific answer, approval, ambiguity ruling, or scope decision is blocking the dependent action. List it under 'Needs you' in CURRENT.md and keep doing independent work that does not need the reply. Post and save the matching open_stops[] item BEFORE setting run to needs_you; name that stop as the owner and record its next poll time (SKILL.md:183-186).
elements.porting_note: Posture::NeedsYou. Requires a persisted open_stops[] id as owner + next_poll_epoch. Independent work may still proceed under working before parking; a stop blocks only actions that depend on its answer (state-machine.md:163-164).

elements.name: Posture/run-state: done
elements.detail: Only after the explicit decision in confirming (SKILL.md:184). Turns off the continuation hook (SKILL.md:198). 'There is no generic idle posture before done' (SKILL.md:203).
elements.porting_note: Posture::Done. Coupled to Phase::Done. This is the only legitimate terminal idle; before it, the harness must be in exactly working/monitoring/needs_you — never a generic idle.

elements.name: Full transition table (authority)
elements.detail: From state-machine.md:116-128. intake->research (else stay for clarification); research->design (else stay while topics remain); design->plan (else stay on ambiguity stop); plan->implement (else stay while incomplete); implement->review at slice boundary (else stay while tasks remain; ->plan if no plan/cursor); review->cr (else stay while fixing; stop at attempts>=stuck_threshold); cr->implement when another slice remains (else stay while CRs open; ->confirming only when plan exhausted AND all CRs terminal); confirming->done only after [A] (->research on [B]; invariant repair to cr/implement/plan; stay on [C]/no reply); done->none (->research only for new user ask). 'No other transition is valid. In particular, cr -> done is forbidden.'
elements.porting_note: Encode as an explicit allowlist transition function `fn can_transition(from, to, guards) -> bool`. Reject everything not listed; hard-code the cr->done prohibition. Guards needed: topics_remain, plan_incomplete, slice_boundary_reached, tasks_remain, plan_or_cursor_missing, review_fixing, attempts>=stuck_threshold, crs_open, plan_exhausted, all_crs_terminal, another_slice_remains, confirm_decision in {A,B,C,repair}.

elements.name: confirming decision options [A]/[B]/[C] + invariant repair
elements.detail: The confirming phase is resolved by an explicit lettered user reply (state-machine.md:125; stop type in SKILL.md:366). [A] = explicit accept -> phase done + posture done. [B] = new direction -> research. [C] (or no reply) = stay in confirming. Separately, an invariant-repair finding can route back to cr, implement, or plan. Never infer approval from silence (SKILL.md:367; state-machine.md example applies).
elements.porting_note: Model as ConfirmDecision enum {Accept, NewDirection, NotYet, RepairTo(Phase)}. Silence/timeout must map to NotYet (stay), never Accept. The repair target must be one of {Cr, Implement, Plan}.

elements.name: review_state / stuck_threshold (durable retry)
elements.detail: state.review_state = {slice_id, signature, attempts, updated_at} (state-machine.md:242-249). Store before each fix; clear only when the problem passes verification or the slice is abandoned. With stuck_threshold:3, the third failed fix stops (attempts>=3) (state-machine.md:253-254; SKILL.md:363-364). Exactly ONE review_state exists because verification fixes run one at a time; if several review units fail, pick deterministically (oldest last_polled, then id), leave others in CR status, don't start their fix loops until review_state clears (state-machine.md:256-259).
elements.porting_note: Single Option<ReviewState> in state, not a map. Increment attempts per fix attempt; compare >= config.stuck_threshold to raise a stop (posture needs_you) while staying in review. Deterministic selection: sort candidates by (last_polled asc, id asc).

elements.name: 'One pass' boundary = one meaningful unit + durable checkpoint gate
elements.detail: A pass is: do ONE meaningful unit of the next dependency-ready local action, then close the durable checkpoint gate BEFORE starting/dispatching another task, advancing phase, posting status, or yielding (SKILL.md:250-348; state-machine.md:155-188 progress loop). Gate steps (SKILL.md:265-329): 1 determine resulting posture/owner/next action; 2 batch all non-run state.json fields into one pm-set.sh call; 3 keep run WORKING until step 11 so the Stop hook protects the partial checkpoint; 4 rewrite CURRENT.md; 5 regenerate handoff.md; 6 append one progress.md entry only for material change; 7 append new source-attributed decisions to decisions.md; 8 compact + pm-validate.sh; 9 seal via pm-checkpoint.sh (kind); 10 recompute pm-due (poll-only bookkeeping invalidates the seal -> re-seal no-change); 11 persist resulting posture via pm-harness.sh as the FINAL mutation (harness rejects missing/stale seal); 12 validate again. Continue in the same entry only when the checkpointed posture is working (state-machine.md:182).
elements.porting_note: This defines the tick boundary of the Rust loop: execute_unit() -> checkpoint() -> recompute_due() -> set_posture(). Keep posture=working across the whole gate; the final posture write is the only place it may flip to monitoring/needs_you/done. Order matters: state files and Markdown ledgers are NOT one atomic transaction (SKILL.md:346-348) — write operation intents before side effects and reconcile on re-entry.

elements.name: Checkpoint seal kinds
elements.detail: material = real change from an important task/result; no-change = a wake that changed nothing or a re-seal of poll-only bookkeeping (cannot substitute for the Markdown updates an important task requires); baseline = created ONCE by the harness on first activation, coordinators never make another; journal = ONLY for heartbeat + status-post infrastructure (state.session, heartbeat/post operations[], channel_state[].last_posted) — journal rejects any other workflow-state/Markdown change, operation deletion/identity rewrite, or backward post timestamp (SKILL.md:284-307).
elements.porting_note: Enum SealKind {Material, NoChange, Baseline, Journal}. Baseline is harness-only at first activation. journal seals add no progress entry and permit a narrow same-engine heartbeat re-registration (job_id may change only if a completed heartbeat op's remote_id equals the new job_id and registered_at moves strictly forward).

elements.name: Run-state controller (pm-harness.sh set) signature
elements.detail: Never edit state.run directly; use the controller (SKILL.md:189-201). Signature: `set <posture> <owner> <wake-condition/next-action> <timestamp>`. Examples: `set working coordinator "execute task-4" -`; `set monitoring CR-1042099 "poll CR-1042099" 1786200900`; `set needs_you stop-publish-4 "wait for stop-publish-4 reply" 1786200900`; `set done - - -`. monitoring and needs_you REQUIRE a next-check timestamp; done turns off the continuation hook; cancel with `pm-harness.sh . cancel`. start and set reject an expired/foreign coordinator lease; set also rejects a foreign Claude session (SKILL.md:198-201).
elements.porting_note: In Rust the daemon is the controller — expose set_posture(posture, owner, next_action, next_check: Option<epoch>) that enforces: monitoring/needs_you require Some(epoch); working uses '-'; validates lease ownership + session identity before writing.

elements.name: Posture-enforcement hooks (Stop + UserPromptSubmit)
elements.detail: Stop hook blocks the session from ending ONLY while state.run.posture==working in the owning session (SKILL.md:14-16). UserPromptSubmit hook coalesces ONLY the exact heartbeat sentinel when the owning session is working under an unexpired lease, and ignores every other prompt returning before reading state (SKILL.md:16-21). Both FAIL OPEN (let the event through) when run is missing/invalid, lease expired/missing, or session foreign; Stop also fails open on corrupt state; the prompt hook still coalesces under a valid working lease even if other state is schema-invalid (SKILL.md:22-28).
elements.porting_note: In the Rust daemon these become internal guards: (a) 'working' is a hard non-yield lock; (b) a scheduled heartbeat that arrives while working is absorbed (coalesced) rather than starting a new pass. Preserve fail-open semantics: missing/invalid lease or foreign session => do not block.

elements.name: Heartbeat sentinel + wake-check
elements.detail: The cron job fires exactly one sentinel: `[project-manager:heartbeat] scheduled wake` (SKILL.md:432-434). Hook calls `pm-harness.sh <root> wake-check <session-id>` (SKILL.md:437-445): if the owning session has a working run with an unexpired lease -> wake is coalesced before reaching model context; a parked/done run, stale/missing lease, recovery state, or foreign session -> let through; the check is READ-ONLY so past-due timestamps stay visible for the required task-boundary pm-due recomputation.
elements.porting_note: wake-check is a pure predicate over (posture, lease validity, session ownership). Only a genuine wake in a parked posture (monitoring/needs_you) with a valid lease starts a new bootstrap pass; heartbeats during working are dropped. Do NOT mutate timestamps in wake-check.

elements.name: Stop triggers (posture -> needs_you)
elements.detail: Stop for (SKILL.md:351-367): missing external-action approval; a genuine ambiguity with multiple defensible answers; validation failure or missing required capability; a worker that fails or exceeds its timeout; verification attempts reaching review_state.attempts >= config.stuck_threshold; project confirmation in confirming. Questions use lettered options plus a free-form escape; never infer approval from silence.
elements.porting_note: Each trigger creates an open_stops[] entry and drives posture->needs_you (except confirmation which is the confirming phase's normal gate). stuck_threshold stop keeps phase=review. Missing REQUIRED capability / validation failure is an ambiguity stop, not a guessed route (state-machine.md:54-55).

elements.name: Bootstrap order (entry gating + initial posture)
elements.detail: Every entry runs 10 ordered steps (state-machine.md:7-112; SKILL.md:39-73): 1 pm-init.sh (init lock); 2 acquire coordinator lease (pm-lock.sh; default config.coordinator_lease_s=7200, must exceed multi_agent.timeout_s by >=60s); 3 pm-validate.sh (older recognizable shape => back up + migrate + reconcile ledgers + delete stale .checkpoint.json then re-validate; unknown corruption => ambiguity stop); 4 pm-harness.sh start => sets state.run to WORKING bound to CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (a well-formed-but-stale seal means a crash: start working and reconcile; a malformed seal blocks activation); 5 read fixed boot set (CURRENT.md, state.json, active phase playbook — CURRENT.md never replaces the playbook, read both); 6 complete intake before detection; 7 detect packages + re-check claude/codex; 8 reconcile pending operations[] + heartbeat liveness (CronList | heartbeat-reconcile -> keep/register/replace); 9 pm-due.sh then enter progress loop; 10 reconcile final checkpoint, persist exit posture, release lease.
elements.porting_note: Every entry (cold start AND every scheduled wake) begins in posture=working after activation, works the progress loop, then parks in exactly one of monitoring/needs_you/done. Bootstrap is idempotent and re-runs on every wake (self-heal). Lease invariant: coordinator_lease_s > multi_agent.timeout_s + 60.

elements.name: Due tracks (what makes phase work runnable)
elements.detail: pm-due.sh returns (SKILL.md:141-160; state-machine.md:131-153): work (advance local phase work; FALSE in done); cr_check (true when due_crs non-empty); due_crs (exact review-unit records due: id, slice_id, kind, branch, packages — a pending draft placeholder with no remote id is never due); comms (stops/experts/status due); due_stops; due_expert_asks; due_async_workers (running opt-in async workers whose poll cadence elapsed; orphaned excluded); posting_allowed (quiet-hours gate for new non-urgent posts; never blocks read-only polling); due_channels. 'The scripts calculate time. Playbooks decide content.'
elements.porting_note: In Rust these are computed fields feeding the progress-loop scheduler. work=false in done is a hard rule. Read-only polling always allowed; only NEW non-urgent posts gate on posting_allowed. Keep the split: harness computes due-ness (time math); phase logic decides the action.

invariants: Legal transitions are EXACTLY the state-machine.md:116-128 table; every other transition is invalid. cr->done is explicitly forbidden (state-machine.md:128).

Phase `done` and posture `done` are coupled and reachable only after an explicit [A] confirmation in the confirming phase (SKILL.md:184; state-machine.md:125). Never infer approval/confirmation from silence (SKILL.md:367).

Posture `working` is a non-yield lock: the session/daemon must not release the coordinator lease or end the pass while working; it always loops within the same entry (SKILL.md:174, 187). The lease is released only from monitoring/needs_you/done.

There is no generic idle posture before done: at any parked point the run is exactly one of monitoring, needs_you, or done; if the phase is not done and none fits, raise an ambiguity stop instead of idling (SKILL.md:184,203-207; state-machine.md:187-188).

monitoring and needs_you MUST record (owner, next-check epoch); done takes none. The posture write is the FINAL mutation of a checkpoint, made via pm-harness.sh, and is rejected on a missing/stale seal or expired/foreign lease (SKILL.md:198-201,327-333).
Run stays `working` across the entire durable-checkpoint gate (steps 1-11) so the Stop hook protects the partial checkpoint; only step 11 flips posture (SKILL.md:268-270,327-328).

A task/unit is not durably complete until the checkpoint gate passes AND the harness accepts its seal; do not announce completion, dispatch the next task, or batch several finished tasks into one later catch-up write (SKILL.md:341-344).
Exactly one review_state exists; verification fixes run one at a time; attempts>=config.stuck_threshold raises a stop without leaving the review phase (state-machine.md:256-259; SKILL.md:363-364).
intake must complete before package/capability detection and before toolchain population (SKILL.md:62; state-machine.md:45-47).
cr->confirming is allowed ONLY when the plan is exhausted AND every CR is terminal; otherwise cr loops back to implement per remaining slice or stays (state-machine.md:124).

Every scheduled wake re-runs the full bootstrap and reconcile (self-heal); state.run.posture starts working on activation and the entry ends by parking in exactly one exit posture (state-machine.md:7-112).
due-track `work` is false whenever phase==done (SKILL.md:144; state-machine.md:132).
gotchas: Two orthogonal state variables are easy to conflate: `state.phase` (intake..done) vs `state.run.posture` (working/monitoring/needs_you/done). Both share the token 'done' but are distinct; only in the confirming->[A] step do phase and posture both become done together.

implement->review is keyed on a SLICE boundary (all of a slice's tasks done), not per-task completion. And implement has a reverse recovery edge implement->plan when no plan/cursor exists (state-machine.md:122).

cr is the loop hub, not a terminal: it cycles cr->implement once per remaining slice. Forgetting the (plan_exhausted && all_crs_terminal) guard would wrongly let cr reach confirming/done early. The validator must hard-reject cr->done.

Hitting stuck_threshold does NOT transition phase — it raises a stop and parks in needs_you while phase stays review (state-machine.md:123). Same pattern for design ambiguity (stays design under a needs_you stop).

The 'one pass' boundary is not one full task — it is one meaningful UNIT followed by a full checkpoint seal; acceptance+integration+verification are normally ONE task-completion checkpoint, split only when a wait/failure/stop/owner change creates a distinct resume state (SKILL.md:261-263).

Poll-only bookkeeping (timers.work or a last_polled cursor) is NOT a new checkpoint but still invalidates the prior seal, forcing a no-change re-seal before parking (SKILL.md:315-326; state-machine.md:174-176). Easy to miss when porting the checkpoint invalidation logic.
Poll cursors move forward and never past the seal time, EXCEPT a CR cursor becomes null in the same material checkpoint that makes the CR terminal (SKILL.md:322-325).

state.json and the four Markdown ledgers are NOT one atomic transaction; write operation intents before side effects and rely on entry-time reconciliation to repair interrupted checkpoints (SKILL.md:346-348). A naive transactional port would be wrong.

The heartbeat sentinel string is exact and load-bearing: `[project-manager:heartbeat] scheduled wake`. The prompt hook matches ONLY this and ignores everything else including the fallback /loop registration command (SKILL.md:432-434, 436-437).

Hooks fail OPEN (let the event through) on missing/invalid run, expired/missing lease, or foreign session — but the prompt hook still coalesces a heartbeat under a valid working lease even when other state is schema-invalid, so a scheduled wake never interrupts protected working work (SKILL.md:22-28).

wake-check is read-only by design so past-due timestamps remain visible for the mandatory task-boundary pm-due recomputation; a port must not 'consume' or clear timestamps during wake-check (SKILL.md:443-445).
baseline seal is harness-only and created exactly once at first activation; coordinators/loop code must never emit another baseline (SKILL.md:290-291).

confirming has an easily-missed fourth outcome beyond [A]/[B]/[C]: an 'invariant repair' escape that routes back to cr, implement, or plan (state-machine.md:125). Model it explicitly, not as part of [C].

area: Early phase playbooks: intake → research → design → plan (project-manager skill, references/phases/)
overview: These four playbooks are the front half of a linear phase machine. Each is a per-phase "brain" the coordinator loads when state.phase matches. intake is a one-time user interview that writes config.json + brief.md; research fans out read-only subagents and persists sourced findings; design and plan delegate to superpowers skills (brainstorming, writing-plans) with auto-waived gates and copy the approved artifact into .project-state/. Every phase ends by writing its owned artifact, doing generic ledger writes (the "Durable checkpoint gate"), and setting state.phase to the next phase — research/design/plan chain within a single coordinator wake, while intake only runs on first start. In the Rust harness, intake stays interactive (harness-owned), and research/design/plan become one-shot stateless worker dispatches whose prompts embed the borrowed playbook text and whose outputs the harness parses and writes to disk.

elements.name: intake — trigger & one-time invariant
elements.detail: Loaded when state.phase=="intake", FIRST START ONLY (intake.md:3-4): 'the coordinator never re-runs intake on a later wake; it reads the confirmed config.json.' Delegates to a short interview with NO external skill. Writes config.json, brief.md, state.channel_state[], and project-scoped state.approvals[]. Advances to state.phase="research" (intake.md:5-8). Goal (intake.md:10-11): capture how the user wants the supervisor to communicate/behave + a confirmed statement of the ask, echoed back so nothing runs silently.
elements.porting_note: Harness-owned interactive flow, not a dispatched worker. Gate on a boolean like config_confirmed / phase!=intake so it never re-enters. Everything downstream reads config.json only.

elements.name: intake Step 1-2 — interview fields & defaults (config.json)
elements.detail: pm-init.sh pre-writes a cold-start config.json; user accepts-all or overrides single lines (intake.md:15-18). Interview table (intake.md:22-33) maps prompt→field→default: scope→brief.md scope (default: current project folder); comms destinations→comms.channels[] each {name,kind,target,role}, kind=slack|file|terminal (default: one slack primary, target asked); per-destination content→comms.channels[].posts (status|stops|cr_activity|decisions|expert_dm) + comms.channels[].audience (free text) (defaults omitted→default routing); update cadence→comms.channels[].update_cadence (default 2h); CR poll cadence→crs[].poll_cadence (default 20m); heartbeat→heartbeat (default 15m); quiet hours→comms.quiet_hours (default none); quiet-hours tz→comms.quiet_hours_tz (default UTC); expert outreach→comms.expert_outreach = ask_first|search_first|ask_only (default ask_first); recurring external actions→state.approvals[] (ask explicitly, no implied approval).
elements.porting_note: Encode as a Rust Config struct with serde defaults matching this table exactly. Reuse the config.schema.json / state.schema.json in references/ verbatim. The prompt table text is borrow-verbatim for the interview UI. Cadences (heartbeat 15m, update 2h, poll 20m) are the wire defaults.

elements.name: intake Step 2 — comms routing rules (posts vs role)
elements.detail: Most projects want one destination: accept default single slack primary, ask target (e.g. #my-project or @me), skip per-destination follow-up (intake.md:37-42). With >1 destination, ASK what each is for, else all classes fan at primary and secondary sits unused (intake.md:44-55). Example: 'team channel gets everything, my manager's DM only wants status' → posts:["status","stops","cr_activity"] on first, posts:["status"]+audience:"my manager — outcomes, not mechanics" on second. CRITICAL (intake.md:52-55): 'role is NOT the answer here — it only picks the fallback destination, so never let a primary/secondary split stand in for what goes where.' Non-configurable cadences: stop polling via comms.stop_backoff keeps default unless raised; expert-DM polling is FIXED by pm-due.sh at hourly for first 24h then every 6h — do not offer as a choice (intake.md:57-64). Fields kept at defaults unless raised: comms.only_on_material_change, cr.publish_approval, stuck_threshold, coordinator_lease_s (intake.md:65-68).
elements.porting_note: Routing is driven by posts[] per channel, with role only as fallback selector. Port a route(content_class)→Vec<channel> resolver that falls back to the role:primary channel when no channel lists that class. Hardcode expert-DM poll schedule (1h×24h then 6h) — not user-configurable.

elements.name: intake Step 3 — confirm scope & the ask (brief.md)
elements.detail: Capture user's original request, every in-scope package/repo path, and confirmed goal+constraints (intake.md:74-79). If the goal has a genuine fork (more than one defensible reading) that is an AMBIGUITY STOP — post lettered options and wait, do not guess. Write result to brief.md (original ask + confirmed goal/constraints); 'This is stable after intake.'
elements.porting_note: brief.md is immutable after intake — a stable input every later phase reads. Ambiguity-stop is the ONLY stop kind intake can raise. Port lettered-option stop mechanism (shared with design).

elements.name: intake Step 4 — explicit external-action approvals
elements.detail: Ask ONE compact lettered question naming exact recurring actions (intake.md:81-91): status/stop posts to each destination; draft CR/PR creation; pushes of project commits and review fixes. Affirmative → separate state.approvals[] entries with action, project/destination scope, granted_by:"user", granted_at, optional expiry. A decline is valid (coordinator asks per-action later). HARD RULE: 'Never request blanket approval for publish, reviewer notification, merge/land, deploy, credentials, payments, or destructive changes.'
elements.porting_note: Model approvals as typed records {action, scope, granted_by, granted_at, expiry?}. The denylist of never-blanket-approvable actions is a load-bearing safety invariant — enforce it in the approval-grant code path, not just the prompt.

elements.name: intake Step 5-6 — write config.json, validate, echo back
elements.detail: Persist answers (incl. accepted defaults) to config.json; write comms.channels[] with target set for slack elements; ensure exactly one role:"primary" (intake.md:93-97). 'Never leave a slack target empty or defaulted — a wrong target sends updates nowhere, silently.' Initialize state.channel_state[] with one {name,last_posted:null} per configured channel. Run pm-validate.sh before leaving intake; post-intake validation REJECTS a missing Slack target or channel-state coverage differing from configured channel set (intake.md:99-103). Step 6 (intake.md:105-116): ALWAYS echo chosen config back even if all defaults accepted — restate each destination name/kind/target, which is primary, what each receives (posts classes, naming default-routed ones, plus audience), the three cadences, quiet_hours; then which recurring external actions were approved vs will stop for per-action approval.
elements.porting_note: Port pm-validate.sh's post-intake checks as a Rust validator that runs before phase leaves intake: (1) every slack channel has non-empty target, (2) exactly one role==primary, (3) channel_state[] names == config channel names. Echo-back is mandatory and is where wrong routing gets caught cheaply — keep it.

elements.name: intake Step 7 — advance & package detection ordering
elements.detail: Set state.phase="research" (intake.md:117-123). Package + capability detection runs from the confirmed scope AFTER intake per state-machine.md; 'it never precedes intake.' Generic ledger writes (CURRENT.md, handoff.md, progress.md, decisions.md, timers) are SKILL.md's Durable checkpoint gate; this playbook OWNS writing config.json + brief.md and setting next phase.
elements.porting_note: Ordering invariant: capability/package detection (populates state.toolchain.packages[]) must be gated to run only after config is confirmed. Unlike research/design/plan, intake does not say 'continue in same entry' — treat intake→research as potentially ending the wake.

elements.name: research — trigger, delegates, artifacts
elements.detail: Loaded when state.phase=="research" (research.md:3). Delegates to built-in Explore subagent(s) for broad read-only search, and builder-mcp search (InternalCodeSearch/InternalSearch/ReadInternalWebsites) for internal code/docs/packages (research.md:4-6). Writes one raw file per topic under .project-state/research/<topic>.md + a short digest + pointers into CURRENT.md. Advances to state.phase="design" (research.md:7-9). Canonical transition authority = state-machine.md (research.md:11). Goal: gather everything design needs and WRITE IT ALL DOWN so nothing is lost to context compaction (research.md:13-14).
elements.porting_note: Harness dispatches read-only worker(s). builder-mcp is Amazon-internal; the port's search backend is pluggable but the two-tier model (direct lookup vs subagent topic) must survive. research/<topic>.md is the durable, compaction-proof store.

elements.name: research Step 1-2 — scope questions & fan-out shape
elements.detail: Step 1 (research.md:19-20): from brief.md, list concrete unknowns design needs (existing patterns, prior art, constraints, affected components); one topic per unknown. Step 2 classification (research.md:22-58): a focused internal-source lookup builder-mcp answers directly is COORDINATOR-OWNED read-only search, NOT counted in fan-out. A topic needing broad exploration/judgment is a subagent topic (seed its prompt from handoff.md). Fan-out by subagent-topic count: 1–2 topics → run scripts/pm-worker.sh ONCE PER TOPIC with PM_WORKER_REQUIRED_SKILL=- and expected tool Agent. 3+ topics → run pm-worker.sh ONCE with expected tool Workflow, prompt uses parallel() over topic list, each topic = one agent() call with structured-output schema, concurrency-capped, coordinator collects/digests/writes. Fallback: Workflow proof missing/unsuccessful → retry topics SEQUENTIALLY via read-only pm-worker.sh calls each requiring one successful Agent result; record this route downgrade in decisions.md with failed Workflow trace as source; if those also unavailable → CAPABILITY STOP.
elements.porting_note: Port the count-based dispatch policy as an enum: OneTopicPerAgent (n≤2) | WorkflowParallel (n≥3) | SequentialFallback. The Rust harness replaces pm-worker.sh/Workflow with its own one-shot dispatcher + a bounded concurrency pool. Preserve: direct-lookup topics not counted; degrade-to-sequential-then-capability-stop ladder. Capability stop is research's stop kind.

elements.name: research Step 2 — parallel() dispatch snippet & schema
elements.detail: Verbatim JS pattern (research.md:40-48): const results = await parallel(topics.map(topic => () => agent(renderPrompt(topic), { label: `research:${topic.id}`, schema: RESULT_SCHEMA }))); return results. Structured-output schema per topic = {summary, findings[], sources[]} (research.md:36). HARD REQUIREMENT (research.md:50-58): 'Writing a subagent topic inline, or only describing the intended calls, does not satisfy this step.' Use the same hard timeout and stream-trace proof as multi-agent.md. Dependent topics (rare) use pipeline() or a follow-up wake (research.md:60-61).
elements.porting_note: RESULT_SCHEMA {summary, findings[], sources[]} is borrow-verbatim as the worker's structured-output contract — define it as a Rust serde struct and require workers to return it. The 'must actually dispatch + prove via stream trace' rule ports to: require a real worker process + captured transcript, reject inline-simulated results.

elements.name: research Step 3 — persist findings with source attribution
elements.detail:
Write full raw output per topic to .project-state/research/<topic>.md — findings, links, code pointers, quotes; do not summarize away detail (research.md:63-66). EVERY finding carries its source (research.md:68-82): one line under the claim naming tool + what it was pointed at (this is the sources[] field carried through to disk — 'don't drop it at digest time'). Verbatim example format:
## Does the pipeline already emit embeddings?
Yes — `EmbeddingWriter.java:88` publishes to the `apollolm-vectors` topic.
*Source: InternalCodeSearch — "apollolm-vectors" · 2026-08-08*
An INFERRED finding must say so (Source: inference from the two findings above); 'an unsourced finding is indistinguishable from a guess.'
elements.porting_note: Borrow-verbatim: the source-line markdown convention (claim, then italic *Source: <tool> — <query> · <date>*) and the inference marker. Enforce in the worker prompt + optionally validate that each finding in findings[] has a non-empty sources[] entry.

elements.name: research Step 4-6 — digest, log forks, advance
elements.detail: Step 4 (research.md:84-85): digest into CURRENT.md — a few lines per topic (answer + pointer to research/<topic>.md). Step 5 (research.md:87-89): log any non-trivial decision/constraint/load-bearing assumption with its source in decisions.md per Durable checkpoint gate. Step 6 (research.md:91-96): set state.phase="design"; generic ledger writes are the Durable checkpoint gate; this playbook OWNS research/*.md + digest + next phase. 'Load design.md and continue through the progress loop in this same entry.'
elements.porting_note: Chaining: after research advances it immediately loads design in the SAME wake. Port the coordinator loop so multiple phases can run per heartbeat until a stop or wait. CURRENT.md is the compact index; decisions.md is the source-attributed decision log (shared across phases).

elements.name: design — trigger, delegate, gate
elements.detail: Loaded when state.phase=="design" (design.md:3). Delegates to superpowers:brainstorming (turns ask+research into an approved design) — 'Do not reimplement design; invoke the skill' (design.md:4-5). Writes approved design to .project-state/design.md; advances to state.phase="plan" (design.md:6-7). GATE: auto-waived — 'proceed without a phase-gate stop unless a hard/ambiguity/stuck rule trips' (design.md:8-9). Goal: produce an approved design grounded in brief.md and research/ findings (design.md:15-16).
elements.porting_note: New repo has zero skill runtime dependency, so the harness must EMBED the brainstorming brain as worker prompt text (or instruct worker to invoke the skill if present). Adapt (not verbatim): the brainstorming flow = clarify intent → propose approaches with trade-offs → present design (design.md:23-25). Auto-waived gate = no user approval stop; harness proceeds automatically.

elements.name: design Step 1-2 — assemble context & land design.md
elements.detail: Step 1 (design.md:19-20): follow CURRENT.md links to brief.md and ONLY the research files the design needs; 'Do not load unlinked files.' Step 2 (design.md:22-28): make the actual Skill tool call, let it run (clarify intent, propose approaches w/ trade-offs, present design). It normally writes to docs/superpowers/specs/…; the supervisor's authoritative copy MUST land at .project-state/design.md (copy/save there + link from CURRENT.md). 'A waived gate still needs a record — planning and later resumes load design.md through that link.'
elements.porting_note: Key porting rule: regardless of where the worker/skill writes, the harness must copy the approved design to .project-state/design.md and register the link in CURRENT.md. Context-minimization ('do not load unlinked files') ports to: seed worker prompt only with CURRENT.md-linked files.

elements.name: design Step 3-5 — stops, log, advance
elements.detail: Step 3 stops (design.md:30-39): NEVER stop to ask 'approve this design?' (gate auto-waived). Stop ONLY on a real trigger: (a) AMBIGUITY STOP — genuine fork with >1 defensible answer → post lettered options and wait (resolve trivial forks without a decision-log entry); (b) HARD STOP — design implies irreversible/risky action (auth/secrets/payments, deletes, deploy) → stop and ask; (c) STUCK STOP — brainstorming can't converge past config.stuck_threshold failed attempts → stop and ask (threshold semantics in review.md). Step 4 (design.md:41-43): record only source-attributed non-trivial design decisions (chosen approach+why, rejected alternatives) in decisions.md. Step 5 (design.md:45-49): set state.phase="plan"; playbook owns design.md + next phase; 'Load plan.md and continue through the progress loop in this same entry.'
elements.porting_note: Three stop kinds for design: ambiguity, hard, stuck (NOT phase-gate). Port stuck_threshold as a per-phase failed-attempt counter with semantics defined in review.md (another slice). Hard-stop trigger list (auth/secrets/payments/deletes/deploy) is load-bearing safety — enforce.

elements.name: plan — trigger, delegate, gate
elements.detail: Loaded when state.phase=="plan" (plan.md:3). Delegates to superpowers:writing-plans (turns approved design into a task-by-task implementation plan) — 'Do not reimplement planning; invoke the skill' (plan.md:4-5). Writes plan to .project-state/plan.md; advances to state.phase="implement" (plan.md:6-7). GATE: auto-waived — 'the skill runs at max autonomy; proceed unless a hard/ambiguity/stuck rule trips' (plan.md:8-9). Goal (plan.md:15-17): produce the task list that becomes the task_cursors[] source AND defines CR slice boundaries, saved where implement and later resumes can read it.
elements.porting_note: Same as design: embed writing-plans brain as worker prompt (zero skill dependency). plan.md is dual-purpose — both the task_cursors[] seed and the CR-slice-boundary definition; the harness parses tasks + slice groups out of it.

elements.name: plan Step 2 — VERBATIM planning instructions (vertical slices + program design)
elements.detail: Step 2 (plan.md:22-40): make the actual Skill call; it writes to docs/superpowers/plans/…; authoritative copy MUST land at .project-state/plan.md. TWO explicit instructions 'because models default the wrong way on both': (1) VERTICAL SLICES, NOT STACK-ORDER LAYERS — 'A slice = the thinnest end-to-end change that a human can pull up and touch (mock API → wire UI → real data → business logic → error handling). NOT (migrations → services → API → frontend), which produces a 2000-line PR nobody can review.' (2) PROGRAM DESIGN BEFORE CODE — 'Any non-trivial task carries a call-stack tree diff, file-tree diff, or type/signature block in the plan — the shape of the code, not just its acceptance criteria. This catches shotgun-surgery habits (try/catch everything, any casts, N duplicated queries) while it is still cheap to change your mind.'
elements.porting_note: BORROW-VERBATIM into the plan worker's prompt: both bullet blocks (plan.md:33-40). These are the load-bearing 'brain' corrections that make the plan reviewable and CR-sliceable. Keep the exact examples (mock API→wire UI→...; call-stack/file-tree/type-signature diff).

elements.name: plan Step 3 — wire plan into control state (task_cursors + CR boundaries)
elements.detail: Step 3 (plan.md:42-51): plan.md task list is source of truth for two mechanisms. (a) task_cursors[] — LEAVE IT [] at the phase transition. Implement reserves the first task or parallel group in the dispatch checkpoint, then removes entries only after acceptance and digest; a resuming coordinator reconciles every reserved entry before redispatching. (b) CR slice boundaries — the plan's phases/checkpoints are the natural CR boundaries; each CR maps to a coherent, independently-reviewable group of tasks (kept small); the implement/cr loop cuts one branch per slice and records it in state.crs[]; 'do not pile the whole plan into one giant CR.'
elements.porting_note: Port task_cursors[] as a reservation queue (empty at plan→implement handoff; implement pops/reserves; entries cleared post-accept+digest; resume reconciles reserved). CR slices = groups of plan tasks → one branch each → state.crs[] record. The 'small CR, not one giant CR' rule is a planning invariant.

elements.name: plan Step 4 — optional non-default dispatch annotations
elements.detail: Step 4 (plan.md:53-94): default route = one Claude subagent per task through a bounded orchestration envelope, sequential, from resolved package cwd. Optional per-task annotation lines (semantics in multi-agent.md): Agent: claude (default, omit) | codex (mechanical transform / non-interactive review via `codex exec`). Isolate: yes → run through blocking CLI in a dedicated git WORKTREE for github, or on the slice BRANCH in existing workspace for brazil ('a worktree breaks brazil-build'; two tasks on same Brazil package can't run in parallel). Parallel with: <task-id>[,...] → declares independence so coordinator MAY fan out concurrently; github tasks get private task branches/worktrees merged sequentially into the slice branch, brazil tasks sharing a package stay sequential; 'Only annotate disjoint changes.' Package: <packages[].name> → the state.toolchain.packages[] element the task centers on; coordinator resolves name→path and launches worker IN THAT FOLDER so the package's CLAUDE.md/.claude/skills/.claude/hooks/ and Codex's AGENTS.md take effect; multiple packages comma-separated (first=cwd, rest via --add-dir); omit only for genuinely project-global tasks. Async: yes → detached async worker (requires Agent: codex + tmux capability); coordinator launches into tmux, parks monitoring, polls on heartbeat rather than waiting inline; for long-running mechanical changes. Deviations from annotations (tool unavailable / annotation wrong) recorded as source-attributed non-trivial deviation in decisions.md. Tag sparingly on Agent:/Parallel with:, LIBERALLY on Package:.
elements.porting_note: Port annotations as optional fields on the Task struct: agent: Claude|Codex, isolate: bool, parallel_with: Vec<TaskId>, package: Vec<String>, async_: bool. Dispatcher reads them to choose route. Preserve brazil-vs-github isolation asymmetry (worktree for github, branch for brazil; brazil worktree breaks brazil-build). Package→cwd resolution is what activates per-package CLAUDE.md/skills — critical for the borrow-the-project-config behavior.

elements.name: plan Step 5-7 — no approval, log, advance
elements.detail: Step 5 (plan.md:96-98): do NOT ask for plan approval (gate auto-waived); proceed to implement; do not log the waiver or trivial calls. Step 6 (plan.md:99-100): record only source-attributed non-trivial planning decisions (slice/CR boundaries, task ordering, dependencies) in decisions.md. Step 7 (plan.md:102-105): set state.phase="implement" AND confirm state.task_cursors==[]; generic ledger writes are the Durable checkpoint gate; 'Load implement.md and continue in the same entry; its first dispatch checkpoint reserves the first task before invoking a worker.'
elements.porting_note: Advance assertion: task_cursors MUST be [] at plan→implement transition (implement owns reservation). No plan-approval stop exists. Plan can still raise hard/ambiguity/stuck stops per header (plan.md:8-9), but not a gate stop.

invariants: Phase order is strictly linear for this slice: intake → research → design → plan → implement. Each playbook sets state.phase to exactly the next phase as its final step.
intake runs on FIRST START ONLY; the coordinator never re-runs it on later wakes and instead reads the confirmed config.json (intake.md:3-4).
After intake, config.json fields are the sole source of behavior; brief.md is stable/immutable after intake (intake.md:79).
comms.channels[] must contain EXACTLY ONE role:"primary"; every slack channel must have a non-empty, correct target (empty/defaulted target = silent failure) (intake.md:95-97).
Content routing is driven by comms.channels[].posts (classes: status|stops|cr_activity|decisions|expert_dm), NOT by role — role only selects the fallback destination (intake.md:52-55).
state.channel_state[] has exactly one {name,last_posted:null} entry per configured channel; pm-validate.sh rejects any mismatch and any missing slack target post-intake (intake.md:99-103).

Approvals are explicit, typed state.approvals[] records; NEVER request or assume blanket approval for publish, reviewer notification, merge/land, deploy, credentials, payments, or destructive changes (intake.md:89-91).

Every research finding carries a source line (tool + target + date), and inferred findings are explicitly marked; sources must survive from the sources[] schema field all the way to disk (research.md:68-82).

Research must ACTUALLY dispatch subagents/workflow (with hard timeout + stream-trace proof); describing calls inline does not satisfy dispatch. Direct builder-mcp lookups are coordinator work and are NOT counted in fan-out (research.md:22-58).
design and plan gates are AUTO-WAIVED: never stop merely to ask for approval; proceed automatically unless a hard/ambiguity/stuck rule trips (design.md:8-9,30-33; plan.md:8-9,96-98).

A waived gate still requires a durable record: the approved design.md and plan.md must be copied into .project-state/ and linked from CURRENT.md, regardless of where the underlying skill wrote them (design.md:26-28; plan.md:25-26).

task_cursors[] is [] at the plan→implement transition; implement owns reservation and clears entries only after acceptance+digest; resuming coordinator reconciles reserved entries before redispatching (plan.md:44-47,102-104).
CR slices are small, coherent, independently-reviewable task groups derived from plan phases/checkpoints; never one giant CR for the whole plan (plan.md:48-51).

Generic ledger writes (CURRENT.md, handoff.md, progress.md, decisions.md, timers) are SKILL.md's shared 'Durable checkpoint gate'; each playbook additionally OWNS its specific artifact(s) and the next-phase set.
Context minimization: design and plan load only CURRENT.md-linked files, never unlinked ones (design.md:19-20; plan.md:19-20).
gotchas: research/design/plan CHAIN WITHIN A SINGLE COORDINATOR WAKE ('continue ... in this same entry'), so one heartbeat can traverse multiple phases; intake does NOT chain — treat intake→research as possibly ending the wake. The Rust loop must support multi-phase progression per wake until a stop/wait.
Package + capability detection runs AFTER intake from the confirmed scope and never before it (intake.md:117-120). Getting this order wrong (detecting packages during intake) violates the machine.

Expert-DM poll cadence is NOT user-configurable: pm-due.sh fixes it at hourly for the first 24h then every 6h. Do not expose it in the interview (intake.md:61-64). Stop-poll backoff (comms.stop_backoff) IS configurable but defaults unless raised.

Four config fields are intentionally NOT asked in the interview and keep defaults unless the user raises them: comms.only_on_material_change, cr.publish_approval, stuck_threshold, coordinator_lease_s (intake.md:65-68).

Stop kinds differ per phase: intake→ambiguity only; research→capability (on missing/failed Workflow+Agent); design→ambiguity|hard|stuck; plan→hard|ambiguity|stuck (never a gate/approval stop). Porting these into one unified StopKind enum must preserve which phase can emit which.

Research fan-out is COUNT-DRIVEN by subagent-topic count (1–2 = one Agent per topic; 3+ = single Workflow with parallel(); fallback = sequential Agent calls then capability stop). Direct builder-mcp lookups do not count toward the threshold — miscounting changes the dispatch route.

brazil vs github isolation is asymmetric: github tasks isolate via git worktree; brazil tasks isolate via a branch in the existing workspace because a worktree breaks brazil-build. Consequently two tasks on the SAME brazil package can never run in parallel (plan.md:60-68).

The Package: annotation is not cosmetic — resolving name→path and launching the worker in that folder is precisely what makes the package's own CLAUDE.md / .claude/skills / .claude/hooks and Codex AGENTS.md take effect. The instruction is to tag Package: liberally but Agent:/Parallel with: sparingly (plan.md:69-93).

Async: yes requires BOTH Agent: codex AND tmux capability, and switches the coordinator from inline-wait to heartbeat-poll with monitoring parked — a different lifecycle than the default blocking one-shot (plan.md:79-86).

design and plan delegate to superpowers skills (brainstorming, writing-plans) in the source, but the new repo has ZERO skill runtime dependency — the harness must embed these 'brains' as worker prompt text. The plan Step 2 vertical-slices + program-design bullets are the highest-value verbatim borrow; the brainstorming flow is a looser adapt.

Trivial forks are resolved WITHOUT a decisions.md entry; only NON-TRIVIAL, source-attributed decisions get logged (design.md:31-32,41-43; plan.md:99-100). Over-logging trivial calls is explicitly discouraged (plan.md:96-98).

Route downgrades/deviations (research sequential-fallback, plan annotation deviations) MUST be recorded in decisions.md with the failed trace as source — this audit trail is load-bearing for later resumes (research.md:49-53; plan.md:90-92).

area: Late-phase playbooks: implement → review → cr → confirming (+ branch-and-cr)
overview: These are the four terminal phases of the project-manager state machine plus the branch/review-unit control doc. The coordinator NEVER edits code itself; it orchestrates ledger state and dispatches stateless one-shot workers (claude `-p` envelope or `codex exec`) via `scripts/pm-worker.sh`, verifies their repository evidence, and records idempotent operations for every external mutation. `implement` runs TDD workers per task/slice; `review` runs a verification gate (optionally adversarial) with a bounded retry-until-stuck loop; `cr` creates/babysits/publishes review units per repository with hard stops on publish and merge; `confirming` is an always-on human hard-stop that alone can declare the project `done`. Everything is crash-safe via pending-before-action operations, reconcile-before-retry, and durable checkpoints.

elements.name: implement phase — purpose & transitions
elements.detail: Loaded when state.phase=="implement" (implement.md:3). Coordinator owns orchestration + ledger; it NEVER edits implementation files (implement.md:9-10). Writes: code on slice branch or temp GitHub task branches; task-completion digests; state.task_cursors[] (implement.md:11-12). Advances to `review` when the current slice is complete; otherwise continues with the next dependency-ready task in the same entry (implement.md:13-14).
elements.porting_note: Rust: PhaseImplement handler. Model as a loop over task_cursors; on empty+slice-complete set phase=Review. The 'coordinator never edits code' rule is an architectural invariant of the whole harness — the Rust dispatcher spawns claude/codex; it must not shell out to edit files.

elements.name: implement Step 1 — resolve current task/group from task_cursors[]
elements.detail: Read state.task_cursors[] (string[] of plan.md task IDs) and locate each in plan.md (implement.md:21-22). Cases: []=reconcile plan.md/progress.md/commits/acceptance-tests; if slice complete advance to review else seed first unfinished dependency-ready task (implement.md:24-26). One entry=execute sequential task. Multiple entries=must form ONE valid `Parallel with:` group (implement.md:27-28). A cursor WITHOUT a completion digest may be an interrupted blocking worker — inspect branch state before redispatching. Count a task complete only when its digest names task+commit+acceptance-test evidence (implement.md:30-32).
elements.porting_note: task_cursors: Vec<String> of task IDs, default []. Completion is NOT tracked by a boolean — it is proven by a digest naming (task_id, commit_ref, test_evidence). Port the reconciliation as a distinct code path triggered whenever a cursor lacks a digest.

elements.name: implement Step 2 — confirm/cut slice branch
elements.detail: Every affected toolchain.packages[] element records the slice branch in active_branch. All null → run Cut-a-branch. Some set/some null → finish Cut-a-branch for missing packages. All set → reuse (implement.md:34-40). Do NOT dispatch until each branch command and pending branch operation is reconciled. NEVER recreate an existing slice branch with `checkout -b` (implement.md:42-43).
elements.porting_note: See branch-and-cr element for the procedure. Key invariant to enforce in Rust: at most one branch per slice_id; guard `git checkout -b` behind an existence check.

elements.name: implement Step 3 — prepare dispatch (worker route selection)
elements.detail: Read Agent:, Isolate:, Parallel with:, Package:, Async: annotations, apply multi-agent.md (implement.md:45-47). Routes: (a) Default = one bounded Claude envelope making one fresh `Agent` call. (b) Valid all-Claude parallel group = one bounded Claude envelope making one actual `Workflow` call with one agent() per isolated member. (c) Mixed or all-Codex parallel group = run members sequentially through their bounded CLI route and RECORD THE DOWNGRADE. (d) `Async: yes` = do NOT issue blocking pm-worker.sh; use detached async worker route. (e) No usable worker route = raise a CAPABILITY STOP, do not implement inline (implement.md:48-61). Resolve Package: against toolchain.packages[]; first package is worker cwd. For GitHub parallel work create one task branch/worktree per (task,repository) but FIRST persist deterministic pending `task-worktree:<repo>:<slice_id>:<task_id>`; reconcile against `git worktree list` + branch ref before retry, complete only when both ready. Brazil tasks stay in existing checkouts; tasks sharing a package run sequentially (implement.md:63-69).
elements.porting_note: Route selection is a match on annotations + detected capabilities (toolchain.capabilities: claude/codex/tmux/gh/...). Downgrade path (c) must write a source-attributed decisions.md entry. Operation key format is load-bearing: `task-worktree:<repo>:<slice_id>:<task_id>`. Port capabilities as a struct of bools.

elements.name: implement Step 3 — worker prompt construction (ADAPT, one verbatim requirement)
elements.detail: Regenerate handoff.md, then build the worker prompt from: goal, constraints, acceptance criteria, branch context, binding decisions, and relevant pointers. Claude's FIRST implementation instruction is to invoke `superpowers:test-driven-development` (implement.md:71-74). Every Claude worker invokes superpowers:test-driven-development via the Skill tool BEFORE editing (implement.md:6-8).
elements.porting_note: The prompt CONTENT is ADAPT (assemble from brief.md/plan.md/decisions.md fields). The requirement that the worker's first action calls superpowers:test-driven-development is VERBATIM/load-bearing and is machine-enforced (see pm-worker.sh element). In the Rust port, this becomes prompt text injected into the claude worker + a post-hoc trace validator. Codex workers have no equivalent skill call (see async trust model).

elements.name: implement Step 4 — checkpoint then invoke pm-worker.sh
elements.detail: Before calling worker: ensure every dispatched task ID is in task_cursors[]; record branch/worktree topology + immediate action in CURRENT.md and handoff.md; append dispatch entry to progress.md; close SKILL.md's material Durable checkpoint gate (implement.md:76-83). Then call `PM_COORDINATOR_RUN_ID=<run-id> scripts/pm-worker.sh` with the selected Claude/Codex route and WAIT for return. The runner renews+verifies the lease, enforces the hard timeout, and for Claude REJECTS a trace without successful matched results for BOTH the required Agent/Workflow call AND the exact superpowers:test-driven-development Skill call. 'A prompt that merely says "delegate this" is not a dispatch.' (implement.md:85-90).
elements.porting_note: pm-worker.sh is the dispatch primitive to reimplement in Rust: spawn claude/codex subprocess, renew coordinator lease (coordinator_lease_s=7200 default), enforce per-worker hard timeout (multi_agent.timeout_s=1800 default) shorter than the lease, and for claude parse the stream-json trace to confirm required tool calls actually succeeded. Cursors MUST be persisted before dispatch (crash-safety).

elements.name: implement Step 5 — verify & integrate the return
elements.detail: 'A worker's success claim is not proof.' Confirm: expected commit/task-scoped diff exists; changed files stay within task scope; required tests added and pass; acceptance criteria satisfied (implement.md:92-98). For a parallel GitHub group: merge task branches into each repo's slice branch SEQUENTIALLY in plan order; persist `merge-task:<repo>:<slice_id>:<task_id>` pending before each merge, complete only after verification; STOP the group on conflict (implement.md:100-103). If evidence missing / call fails / repo contradicts return → keep the cursor and raise `worker_stuck` stop (from multi-agent.md); preserve captured output and partial commits (implement.md:105-107).
elements.porting_note: Repository-evidence verification is the acceptance gate (NOT exit code / self-claim) — this is reused verbatim by the async route too. Merge ordering + per-merge operation key `merge-task:<repo>:<slice_id>:<task_id>` is load-bearing. worker_stuck stop schema in the stops element below.

elements.name: implement Step 6 — digest & advance
elements.detail: Prepare ONE concise completion digest: task IDs, changes, tests, commit refs, follow-ups. A parallel group returning together gets ONE group digest (implement.md:109-112). Remove only accepted+digested task IDs from task_cursors[], then: unfinished slice → seed next dependency-ready task/group; complete slice → set state.phase="review" and load review.md (implement.md:114-117). Close material Durable checkpoint before dispatching successor or entering review. CURRENT.md/handoff.md/progress.md must describe completed task + next action. Record only source-attributed non-trivial forks/corrections/rulings in decisions.md. After the checkpoint, rerun `pm-due` and service newly due tracks before the successor dispatch. Same boundary applies after a failed/timed-out/stuck worker once its stop checkpoint is durable (implement.md:119-125).
elements.porting_note: Digest is the completion proof consumed by Step 1 reconciliation. 'rerun pm-due and service newly-due tracks' = after each material checkpoint the scheduler re-evaluates due CRs/stops/async-workers before continuing — port pm-due as a scheduler query returning due_crs/due_stops/due_async_workers.

elements.name: implement Step 7 — conservative interrupted-task recovery
elements.detail: On a later entry, any cursor without a digest triggers reconciliation: inspect task+slice branches/worktrees; compare commits+changed files with acceptance criteria; verify tests; accept+digest complete work; preserve partial work and redispatch ONLY missing criteria; retry the full task only when no trustworthy work exists (implement.md:127-136). 'Never assume a dead subprocess made no repository changes.' (implement.md:137). Same 6-step recovery restated in multi-agent.md:339-354.
elements.porting_note: Critical crash-recovery invariant for the Rust port: a killed worker may have left commits. Always inspect git state before redispatch. This is why cursors are written pre-dispatch.

elements.name: implement Step 8 — honor stops
elements.detail: Stop before risky external actions and on genuine implementation ambiguity. Post lettered options through the configured stop destination, persist the operation intent before posting, keep the stop visible in CURRENT.md. Continue independent work when available. Set harness run to `needs_you` only after the stop is durable AND no independent action remains (implement.md:139-144).
elements.porting_note: needs_you is a run.posture value; only enter it when stop is persisted and nothing else is runnable. Model 'independent work continues' — a stop on one task does not halt disjoint runnable work.

elements.name: implement — Async worker route (opt-in, codex+tmux only)
elements.detail: Async: yes requires Agent: codex AND tmux capability (multi-agent.md:270-271). Do NOT issue blocking pm-worker.sh. Launch (material checkpoint): (1) persist pending `async-launch:<task_id>`; (2) `tmux new-session -d -s pm-aw-<id>` running codex WRAPPED so on exit it writes exit code to worker's done_signal file and pipes stdout/stderr to log file; (3) complete operation; (4) append async_workers[] element with deadline=started_at+config.multi_agent.async_timeout_s (frozen, independent of lease); (5) close material checkpoint (multi-agent.md:286-296). Park: with a running worker and nothing else runnable, set run=monitoring (owner=worker id, next-check=poll cadence) and release the lease (multi-agent.md:298-301). Poll (heartbeat): for each id in due_async_workers gather `tmux has-session` (alive?) + `test -f done_signal` (present?), call `pm-async.sh <ps> poll <id> <alive 0|1> <done 0|1> <now>` → verdict running/done/orphaned. running=advance last_polled only (no progress.md entry). done=read exit code+log, VERIFY branch/diff/tests exactly as blocking return, then digest + `tmux kill-session` + remove async_workers[] element + material checkpoint. orphaned (session_gone or deadline_exceeded)=kill-session if alive, set element status:orphaned (material), raise worker_stuck stop with log as evidence (multi-agent.md:303-318). Trust model: no stream-json trace validator for async; exit code 0 does NOT accept — repository evidence does (multi-agent.md:326-330).
elements.porting_note: pm-async.sh is a PURE decision function (never touches tmux/fs/state) — port as a Rust fn(record, alive:bool, done:bool, now)->Verdict; coordinator does all tmux + state writes. Only route that produces run.posture=monitoring. `done` always wins races (multi-agent.md:320-324). async_timeout_s default 3600.

elements.name: review phase — purpose & transitions
elements.detail: Loaded when state.phase=="review" (review.md:3). Delegates to superpowers:verification-before-completion (the gate proving the slice works); on verification failure delegates to superpowers:systematic-debugging to diagnose and a bounded worker implements the fix; count attempts against config.stuck_threshold (review.md:4-7). Writes: worker fixes on slice active_branch; state.review_state for every fix attempt; verification evidence + any stuck stop to ledger (review.md:8-11). Advances to state.phase="cr" on PASS; when repeated failure reaches threshold triggers the STUCK STOP (halt and ask) instead of advancing (review.md:12-13). Goal: no slice is 'done' on 'seems right' — advances to cr only with evidence (tests pass, build green, runtime check) (review.md:17-18).
elements.porting_note: Rust PhaseReview handler. Delegated skills become worker-prompt requirements enforced by pm-worker.sh's required-skill validator (PM_WORKER_REQUIRED_SKILL). stuck_threshold default 3 lives in config.json.

elements.name: review Step 1 — verification gate + conditional adversarial verify
elements.detail: Make the actual verification-before-completion Skill call, then run its full verification against the slice on active_branch: acceptance criteria of every task in current plan.md checkpoint, the build, and the test suite. Result is PASS (evidence) or FAIL (concrete reproduced problem) (review.md:22-27). CONDITIONAL adversarial verify via Workflow tool for slices touching RISKY SURFACE: run pm-worker.sh with PM_WORKER_REQUIRED_SKILL=- and expected tool Workflow; its prompt uses pipeline() to fan out N adversarial verifiers per finding, each told to REFUTE with a distinct lens (correctness/security/repro) (review.md:29-35). Trigger conditions (ANY): slice modifies files matching auth/session/token/crypto/payment patterns (hard-stops list in SKILL.md); ships a DB migration/schema change; changes a public API or anything the always-on hard-stop model treats as irreversible (review.md:43-49). For ordinary slices single-pass verification is enough (adversarial costs 3× verify wake tokens) (review.md:51-53). When adversarial runs: any finding a MAJORITY of lenses refute is dropped from the failure set; record verifier evidence in ledger; sourced decision only when dropping is a non-trivial ruling; survivors go to Step 3 as normal failures (review.md:53-56). Fallback: if the bounded Claude trace lacks a successful Workflow result, run verifier lenses SEQUENTIALLY through read-only pm-worker.sh calls each requiring one successful Agent result, record source-attributed downgrade in decisions.md; if those unavailable raise a capability stop (review.md:57-61).
elements.porting_note: Risky-surface detection = regex match on changed file paths (auth|session|token|crypto|payment) OR migration/schema OR public-API/irreversible. Port as a predicate over the slice diff. Majority-refute drop rule: count lens verdicts, drop finding if >50% refute. The pipeline() block is DSL pseudocode (ADAPT) but the per-agent instruction text is near-verbatim (see next element).

elements.name: review — adversarial verify prompt snippets (mixed verbatim/adapt)
elements.detail:
Workflow DSL pseudocode (review.md:37-42):
```
pipeline(findings, f =>
  parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>
    agent(`Try to refute: ${f.summary}. Lens: ${lens}. Default refuted=true if uncertain.`,
          {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA}))))
```
elements.porting_note: The pipeline()/parallel()/agent() structure is ADAPT — it is the Claude Workflow-tool DSL; the Rust harness instead fans out N codex/claude one-shot verifier calls per finding. The per-verifier instruction string 'Try to refute: <finding summary>. Lens: <correctness|security|repro>. Default refuted=true if uncertain.' should be borrowed near-VERBATIM as the verifier prompt. Each returns a VERDICT_SCHEMA object (refuted:bool + rationale).

elements.name: review Step 2 — on PASS advance
elements.detail: Record verification evidence. If a fix worker ran, verify+digest its accepted return then remove its task cursor. Clear state.review_state, set state.phase="cr", load cr.md, and continue through the progress loop in the SAME entry (review.md:63-66).
elements.porting_note: On pass: review_state=null, phase=Cr, then fall through to cr handling in the same wake (no early return).

elements.name: review Step 3 — on FAILURE: diagnose, reserve, dispatch, count
elements.detail: Invoke superpowers:systematic-debugging via Skill tool. Reproduce failure and identify the owning task in current slice's plan.md (review.md:68-70). Compute a short `signature` from the failing test/error. review_state record (review.md:75-82, state-schema.md:193-202): {"slice_id":"slice-2","signature":"test_checkout_totals","attempts":1,"updated_at":<epoch>}. Before each fix reconcile review_state + task_cursors[]: reuse a matching owning-task cursor from an interrupted/failed attempt, else reserve that task in an EMPTY cursor set; reconcile any unrelated cursor first. A different slice_id OR signature starts at attempts:1; the SAME problem increments attempts. Persist retry record + cursor in the pre-dispatch checkpoint so a crash cannot reset either (review.md:84-89). Build a fix prompt from diagnosis + task acceptance criteria + active branch; dispatch via pm-worker.sh per multi-agent.md. Coordinator may diagnose/inspect diff/verify/digest but must NOT edit implementation locally. Keep the cursor until worker return accepted+digested. Re-run verification after worker returns: pass→Step 2; fail→Step 4 using the persisted attempt count (review.md:91-99).
elements.porting_note: review_state: Option<ReviewState{slice_id:String, signature:String, attempts:u32, updated_at:i64}>. attempts keying is by (slice_id, signature) — changing either resets to 1. This is a top-level singleton (exactly one active failure), NOT a per-task map — serializes all fix loops across review AND cr phases.

elements.name: review Step 4 — stuck threshold semantics
elements.detail: Stop when failed attempts >= config.stuck_threshold. With default 3: first and second failed fixes may retry; the THIRD failed fix STOPS (review.md:101-104). On resume, if the unresolved record is already at/above threshold, POST/RECONCILE the existing stuck stop instead of attempting another fix (review.md:104-105). The stuck message names the problem + attempted fixes and offers lettered options. Persist its post as a `pending` state.operations[] intent before posting, then complete/reconcile per state-machine.md idempotent-operations. Do NOT clear state.review_state while the problem awaits input (review.md:107-111).
elements.porting_note: Threshold check: `attempts >= stuck_threshold` (so default 3 stops on the 3rd failure). On cold resume, check this BEFORE dispatching to avoid a 4th attempt. Stuck stop is a comms post gated by a pending post operation.

elements.name: review Steps 5-6 — clear on resolution, record outcome
elements.detail: Remove state.review_state and its fix cursor when verification passes OR the slice is explicitly abandoned; a new signature replaces the retry record per Step 3 (review.md:113-115). Put verification evidence + failed attempts in the ledger; add decisions.md entry only for a source-attributed non-trivial ruling; keep a stuck stop auditable: what failed, what was tried N times, why work halted (review.md:117-120).
elements.porting_note: review_state cleared ONLY on pass or explicit abandon — never on a mere retry. Ledger writes (CURRENT.md/handoff.md/progress.md/timers) are the generic Durable checkpoint gate owned by SKILL.md, not this phase.

elements.name: cr phase — purpose & transitions
elements.detail: Loaded when state.phase=="cr" (cr.md:3). Delegates to `cr-babysit` for Brazil/CRUX and `gh` for GitHub (cr.md:4). Writes: one draft review + one state.crs[] entry per review unit; task cursors + worker digests for implementation fixes; operation intents for every external mutation (cr.md:5-7). Goal: create and babysit every review unit for the verified slice without duplicating remote actions after a crash (cr.md:11-12). This phase NEVER sets phase="done" (cr.md:125).
elements.porting_note: Rust PhaseCr handler. External-tool coupling is heaviest here — cr-babysit (an installed skill) and gh CLI. In the standalone harness, cr-babysit's polling logic must be reimplemented or invoked as a worker; gh is a subprocess.

elements.name: cr Step 1 — partition slice into review units
elements.detail: Use slice's stable slice_id, tasks, packages, branch, base (cr.md:15-16). Brazil packages MAY share one multi-package CR (no per-repo split). GitHub packages grouped by repository — each repository gets its own PR. A mixed slice produces one Brazil CR PLUS one PR per GitHub repository (cr.md:17-21). Every crs[] entry carries the shared slice_id; locate an existing entry by slice_id PLUS repository/package group, NOT by branch alone (cr.md:23-24). (Restated branch-and-cr.md:58-72.)
elements.porting_note: Review-unit partitioning: group by kind — one CR for all Brazil packages in the slice; one PR per GitHub repo. crs[] entry lookup key = (slice_id, package-group), never branch alone (branches are shared across a slice).

elements.name: cr Step 2 — reconcile before creating (draft-cr operation key)
elements.detail: For each missing entry inspect its deterministic operation key. Build <review-unit> by SORTING crs[].packages, URI-escaping each package name, joining with `+`; full key = `draft-cr:<review-unit>:<slice_id>` (cr.md:27-30). States: completed → recover its remote id + ensure matching crs[] entry exists; pending → query CRUX/GitHub for the draft before retry; failed → query CRUX/GitHub, complete existing op if draft exists else reset that same record to pending before retry; absent → verify the approval required by state-machine.md external-action-approvals, then persist op as pending (cr.md:31-38). A crash-recovery crs[] placeholder may have id:null ONLY while that matching operation is pending; keep status:"draft", last_polled:null; not pollable until reconciliation records the remote ID (cr.md:40-43).
elements.porting_note: Operation key construction is EXACT and load-bearing: sort packages, percent-encode each name, join with '+', prefix `draft-cr:`, suffix `:<slice_id>`. Port as a deterministic key fn shared by pending/complete/reconcile. Draft creation requires an approval check (config.cr.publish_approval etc.).

elements.name: cr Step 3 — create drafts (Brazil vs GitHub)
elements.detail: Brazil: invoke cr-babysit ONCE with every Brazil package in the review unit and OMIT publish (cr.md:46-47). GitHub: first PUSH each repo's slice branch — persist `push:<repo>:<head-commit>` pending, complete after remote ref confirmed, reconcile before retry — then `gh pr create --draft --base <base> --head <slice-branch> --fill` (cr.md:48-51). On success atomically append the review unit's crs[] entry AND complete its operation with remote id + completion time. Entry includes slice_id, id, kind, repository identity/package group, branch, base, status:"draft", tasks, last_polled:null (cr.md:53-57). On failure mark operation failed with concise detail (cr.md:58).
elements.porting_note: crs[] element shape (state-schema.md:106-120): {id, slice_id, kind:"brazil"|"github", branch, base, status, tasks:[..], packages:[..], last_polled, poll_cadence?}. gh commands are subprocess calls; cr-babysit must be reimplemented for the standalone harness. Append-entry + complete-operation must be atomic (single state write).

elements.name: cr Step 4 — babysit open reviews (read-only polling + serialized fix loop)
elements.detail: Polling is READ-ONLY. Poll only review units listed in pm-due.sh's due_crs; another due CR never advances a fresh CR's cadence (cr.md:60-62). Brazil: let cr-babysit poll analyzers + reviewer feedback. GitHub: poll `gh pr checks <id>` and review state (cr.md:63-64). Keep babysitting until each async check finishes and the unit reaches its next durable state — starting an analyzer/upload/poll is NOT completion (cr.md:66-68). Fix ONE review unit at a time: diagnose failure, map to an owning task in that unit's crs[].tasks; reuse a matching task cursor from interrupted/failed attempt else reserve owning task in an empty cursor set; persist cursor + state.review_state in pre-dispatch checkpoint; run fix via pm-worker.sh per multi-agent.md on the active review branch (cr.md:70-74). Coordinator may diagnose/inspect/verify/integrate/digest but must NOT edit locally; remove cursor only after return accepted+digested. While review_state non-null continue THAT unit and leave other failures queued in their crs[] status. Among new failures choose by oldest last_polled, then id (cr.md:76-81). Before uploading a CRUX revision or pushing a GitHub commit persist deterministic pending op e.g. `push:<review-unit>:<commit>`, complete after remote confirms, reconcile before retry (cr.md:83-86).
