All review-fix attempts (found here OR in review phase) use top-level state.review_state; stop when attempts>=config.stuck_threshold (default stops after 3rd failed fix) (cr.md:88-92).
elements.porting_note: Fix loop REUSES the same review_state singleton as the review phase — serialized across both phases. Poll cadence gating: only touch CRs in due_crs (per-CR backoff). Tie-break new failures: (oldest last_polled, then id). cr-babysit polling = reimplement analyzer/reviewer status checks; gh pr checks = subprocess.

elements.name: cr Step 5 — publish & land (per-unit HARD STOPS)
elements.detail: When checks green: WITHOUT authorization create the publish stop — persist `post:<channel>:<content-hash>` pending before posting, complete with message id so resume reconciles instead of double-posting. WITH authorization persist `publish:<review-unit>:<revision>` pending then publish (`cr --publish` OR `gh pr ready` plus reviewer requests); complete op and set status:"in_review" only after remote confirmation (cr.md:94-101). Merge/land is a SEPARATE hard stop: after explicit approval record `merge:<review-unit>:<revision>` pending before acting, complete + set status:"landed" only after remote confirmation (cr.md:103-105). Whenever a unit reaches terminal status (landed or abandoned) clear its last_polled to null in the SAME pm-set.sh call; a terminal entry is never polled again, pm-validate.sh rejects a terminal entry that retains a poll cursor (cr.md:107-110). (Also branch-and-cr.md:87-99.)
elements.porting_note: TWO distinct hard stops: publish and merge/land — both per-review-unit, both need explicit user authorization (config.cr.publish_approval e.g. "per_cr"). status lifecycle: draft→in_review→landed (or →abandoned). Terminal ⇒ last_polled=null (validated). Operation keys: post:<channel>:<content-hash>, publish:<review-unit>:<revision>, merge:<review-unit>:<revision>. `cr --publish` / `gh pr ready` are subprocesses.

elements.name: cr Step 6-7 — continue workflow, honor stops (transition to confirming)
elements.detail: Once every review unit for this slice is created+registered: if another slice remains, invoke the slice-branch procedure in branch-and-cr.md before implementation resumes; otherwise remain in `cr` while any review unit is open, then follow the canonical transition to `confirming` (cr.md:112-117). An open review does NOT block a later independent slice ONLY when package sets are disjoint. A package has one active_branch; overlapping independent slices wait until the earlier review is terminal, a dependent slice stacks on its parent's branch. Continue runnable disjoint slices in the same entry; when only remote reviews remain, record `monitoring` with next poll times. This phase NEVER sets phase="done" (cr.md:119-125). Publishing/merge/land/any risky external action use state-machine.md approval rules; an unclear review-unit mapping is an AMBIGUITY STOP; every stop post + external mutation follows pending/completion/reconciliation; never infer success from a crashed command (cr.md:127-131).
elements.porting_note: cr→confirming transition is authored in state-machine.md (not here); cr only advances when all units terminal AND no more slices/tasks. Independent-slice concurrency gate: disjoint package sets only (active_branch is per-package singleton). 'monitoring' posture when only remote polling remains.

elements.name: confirming phase — purpose, fire condition, transitions
elements.detail: Loaded when state.phase=="confirming" (confirming.md:3). Delegates to the comms channel — post the confirm-done stop and poll for the reply via comms.md; a lifecycle gate the coordinator OWNS, not delegated to an installed skill (confirming.md:4-6). Writes: posts confirm-done stop to `primary` comms.channels[] element (auto-degrading to STATUS.md when Slack unreachable); logs outcome to decisions.md; on [B] archives plan.md to archive/plan-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md and appends an Addendum to brief.md (confirming.md:7-11). Advances to: state.phase="done" on [A]; state.phase="research" on [B]; stays in confirming on [C] hold or while no reply yet (confirming.md:12-14). FIRE CONDITION (must be true on entry, RECOMPUTE every entry): (1) plan tasks exhausted — every task in current plan.md completed and rolled into a CR (equivalently task_cursors[] empty and no slice pending); (2) all CRs terminal — state.crs[] non-empty AND every element status ∈ {landed, abandoned} (the same 'open' predicate pm-due.sh uses) (confirming.md:24-31). If either false, arriving here is a resume-safety bug: do NOT post; correct the phase — any CR open→phase="cr"; tasks remain→phase="implement" (or `plan` if task_cursors[] empty AND no plan.md exists yet) (confirming.md:33-38).
elements.porting_note: 'confirming' is the ONLY phase besides research-reentry that can reach `done`. Fire-condition recomputation on every entry is the core resume-safety mechanism — port as a guard that runs first and can bounce the phase back to cr/implement/plan. 'open CR' predicate: status not in {landed, abandoned}.

elements.name: confirming Steps 1-3 — verify fire condition, poll-before-post, post confirm-done stop
elements.detail: Step 1: verify fire condition; if not satisfied correct phase, load that playbook, continue same entry (confirming.md:44-46). Step 2: if the outstanding confirm-done stop ID is in pm-due.sh's due_stops, poll it per comms.md BEFORE posting; if user already replied skip post and jump to Step 4; do not let an unrelated CR-check wake bypass stop backoff (confirming.md:48-51). Step 3: post the confirm-done stop ONCE per outstanding question — if no reply pending and no confirm-done question already outstanding on the channel, require the configured recurring comms approval, write a pending post operation, then post recap + lettered options; complete the operation and append the full open_stops[] constructor from state-schema.md; this hard-stop message is material by definition and NEVER suppressed by only_on_material_change (confirming.md:53-59). 'Wait for the reply. Never assume [A]. Plan exhausted is the coordinator's signal, not the user's — silently going to done is exactly the failure mode this phase exists to prevent.' (confirming.md:61-63). The completed operation + open_stops[] element prevent duplicate posts; CURRENT.md 'Needs you' line names the pending stop (confirming.md:71-72).
elements.porting_note: Duplicate-post prevention = (completed post operation) + (open_stops[] element present). only_on_material_change MUST be bypassed for this hard-stop. Poll-before-post ordering avoids re-posting when a reply already landed. Enforce 'never assume [A]' — timeouts never auto-resolve (Step 5).

elements.name: confirming Step 3 — recap + lettered options (contents required, template ADAPT)
elements.detail: Compose the recap naturally for the configured audience per comms.md: include what shipped, the landed review units, and any explicit out-of-scope items that matter. Then ask whether the project is complete with these choices on SEPARATE LINES: `[A] confirm done`, `[B] more work - describe the ask`, `[C] hold - decide later`. 'These are required contents, not a literal labeled template.' (confirming.md:64-70).
elements.porting_note: The three letter semantics [A]/[B]/[C] and their meanings are VERBATIM/load-bearing (they drive Step 4 branching). The surrounding recap prose is ADAPT — generate from shipped work + landed crs[] + out-of-scope notes. Do not hardcode the exact sentence; DO hardcode the three options + their required contents.

elements.name: confirming Step 4 — act on the reply ([A]/[B]/[C]/no-reply)
elements.detail: [A] confirm done: set phase="done"; log 'user confirmed project complete via [A]' to decisions.md with the stop reply as source; generic checkpoint regenerates handoff.md; later heartbeat wakes remain idle in `done`, user can stop them with state.session.cancel_handle (confirming.md:76-82). [B] more work (reply body is the new ask): append an **Addendum (YYYY-MM-DD)** section to brief.md with user's reply VERBATIM as new ask/constraints (amend, do NOT overwrite — brief.md is the load-bearing goal file every later phase + handoff.md quote from); archive current plan.md to archive/plan-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md; clear state.task_cursors to [] so the new plan seeds it; log 'user requested new scope: <one-line>' to decisions.md with stop reply as source; set phase="research". Pipeline re-enters research→design→plan→implement→review→cr then lands back in confirming. Do NOT shortcut the pipeline for a 'small' ask — research re-surfaces affected code + prior decisions, and a genuinely small ask yields zero research topics and advances quickly. Load research.md and continue this same entry (confirming.md:84-99). [C] hold: keep phase unchanged, set stop status to `held`, record user's choice in decisions.md with stop reply as source, do NOT re-post, poll it on the next wake where its ID appears in due_stops (confirming.md:101-104). No reply yet: record `needs-you` with stop ID + next eligible poll, then exit; poll again only when its ID next appears in due_stops (confirming.md:106-107).
elements.porting_note: [B] loops the whole machine back to research (not a shortcut) — brief.md is APPENDED (Addendum section, verbatim user text), plan.md archived with dated filename, task_cursors cleared. [A] is the only terminal transition. [C] sets stop.status=held (not cleared). Reply free-form body carries the new ask. session.cancel_handle stops the heartbeat cron.

elements.name: confirming Step 5 — honor stop rules (Slack-unreachable fallback)
elements.detail: A hard stop NEVER auto-resolves on a timeout; coordinator never proceeds on a guessed answer. If Slack unreachable, comms.md's Slack-unreachable fallback applies as for the publish stop: the status UPDATE degrades to STATUS.md, but the BLOCKING QUESTION PAUSES. 'A file write is not consent.' (confirming.md:109-113).
elements.porting_note: Critical invariant for the Rust port: degrade status-posting to a local STATUS.md file when Slack is down, but the blocking confirm-done question must PAUSE (cannot be answered by a file). No timeout auto-advance.

elements.name: branch-and-cr — slice branch invariant
elements.detail: Each slice has a stable slice_id and branch name `pm/slice-<N>-<short-slug>`; every package the slice touches records that name in toolchain.packages[].active_branch (branch-and-cr.md:7-11). Same name does NOT imply one checkout: each GitHub repo has its own slice branch (parallel tasks use temporary per-task branches/worktrees, merge into that repo's slice branch in plan order — see multi-agent.md); Brazil packages use existing workspace checkouts, packages sharing one checkout cannot run in parallel (branch-and-cr.md:13-18). If all relevant active_branch null on entry to implement, open the slice before dispatch; if only some null, reconcile the partially opened slice and record the existing branch on remaining packages; NEVER create a second branch for the same slice_id (branch-and-cr.md:20-24).
elements.porting_note: Branch naming is deterministic: `pm/slice-<N>-<short-slug>`. active_branch is a per-package String field. The one-branch-per-slice_id invariant must be guarded. GitHub repos each get their own branch of the same name; Brazil uses existing workspace checkout (no new checkout).

elements.name: branch-and-cr — Cut a slice branch procedure (branch operation key)
elements.detail: (1) Choose base: project base for independent slice, previous slice branch for a dependent/stacked slice (branch-and-cr.md:31-32). (2) Reconcile before acting: for each repo/package checkout look up deterministic key `branch:<package-or-repo>:<slice_id>` — completed→verify branch exists and reuse; pending→inspect checkout+remote, complete record if branch exists, retry only when reconciliation proves it does not; absent→persist pending op BEFORE any fetch/checkout/branch creation (branch-and-cr.md:33-41). (3) Freshen and open each checkout: Brazil `brazil ws sync --md`; GitHub/git fetch + fast-forward the base; if slice branch does not exist create from chosen base, if exists check it out — do NOT run another `checkout -b` (branch-and-cr.md:42-46). (4) Record completion: set each package's active_branch, mark branch op completed with branch/ref + completion time (branch-and-cr.md:47-48). (5) Log the fork: record slice_id, branch, base, independent-vs-stacked in decisions.md citing the plan dependency as source (branch-and-cr.md:49-50). Branch creation, push, CR/PR creation, publish, merge, posts ALL follow pending-before-action + reconcile-before-retry; wait for each command to finish and confirm local/remote state before completing its op record; never treat dispatch as completion (branch-and-cr.md:51-55).
elements.porting_note: Operation key `branch:<package-or-repo>:<slice_id>` per checkout. Base selection: independent=project base, stacked=parent slice branch. Commands: `brazil ws sync --md` (Brazil), git fetch+ff (GitHub). Guard `checkout -b` behind existence check. The universal pending→act→complete/fail→reconcile protocol is the harness's idempotency journal (state.operations[]).

elements.name: branch-and-cr — review units per slice & stacked vs independent
elements.detail: Review units per slice (branch-and-cr.md:58-72): GitHub=one PR + one crs[] entry per repository; Brazil=one multi-package CR + one crs[] entry may span all Brazil packages in the slice; mixed=Brazil unit + one unit per GitHub repo. Every entry carries shared slice_id, while id/branch/base/packages/kind/status/last_polled describe that unit. Review-unit polling MAY be concurrent, but fix loops are SERIALIZED because state.review_state represents exactly one active failure. Stacked vs independent (branch-and-cr.md:74-84): Independent=branch from project base; separate slices in flight concurrently ONLY when package sets disjoint (one active_branch per package, so overlapping independent slices run sequentially). Stacked=branch from the UNLANDED parent slice branch, record that branch as the unit's base; after parent lands, rebase/retarget each child unit and update its base. The dependency graph in plan.md decides; the coordinator does NOT infer new slice boundaries.
elements.porting_note: Concurrency invariants: polling parallel, fix loops serial (single review_state). Independent-slice concurrency requires disjoint package sets. Stacked child's base = parent slice branch until parent lands, then rebase + update base. Do not synthesize slice boundaries — read them from plan.md dependency graph.

elements.name: Stop kinds raised in late phases
elements.detail: worker_stuck (open_stops[].kind:"worker_stuck", multi-agent.md:358-374): raised when a worker call fails/times out, return lacks verification evidence, repo state conflicts with claim, or commit/diff/tests cannot be reconciled; offers [A] retry missing work with fresh worker, [B] retry through alternate blocking surface, [C] show captured result + repo evidence, [D] skip/block task ([D] requires a sourced decisions.md entry); preserve captured output. Also raised by async orphaned verdict with log as evidence. review STUCK STOP: attempts>=config.stuck_threshold (default: 3rd failed fix stops); names problem + attempted fixes + lettered options (review.md:101-111). capability stop: no usable worker route (implement.md:61), Workflow+sequential-Agent fallbacks both unavailable (review.md:61), tmux/codex unavailable for async (multi-agent.md:276-277), task needs background/daemon (multi-agent.md:259-261). cr publish stop + merge/land stop: per-review-unit hard stops needing authorization (cr.md:94-105). cr ambiguity stop: unclear review-unit mapping (cr.md:129). implement ambiguity stop: genuine implementation ambiguity (implement.md:140). confirming confirm-done stop: always-on hard stop, never auto-resolves on timeout (confirming.md:109-111).
elements.porting_note: Model as enum StopKind { WorkerStuck, ReviewStuck, Capability, Publish, Merge, Ambiguity, ConfirmDone }. Each carries lettered options as data. All stops = open_stops[] elements posted to comms with a pending `post:<channel>:<content-hash>` operation. worker_stuck options text is near-verbatim reusable. [D]-style destructive/skip options require a sourced decisions.md entry.

elements.name: pm-worker.sh dispatch contract & required-skill enforcement
elements.detail: Invocation: `PM_COORDINATOR_RUN_ID=<run-id> scripts/pm-worker.sh <route>` (implement.md:86). Runner responsibilities: renew + verify the coordinator lease; enforce a hard per-worker timeout (< coordinator lease). For CLAUDE: reject a trace lacking successful matched results for BOTH the required orchestration call (Agent or Workflow) AND the exact required Skill call (implement.md:87-90). PM_WORKER_REQUIRED_SKILL env selects the enforced skill: superpowers:test-driven-development for implement; `-` (none) for the adversarial-verify Workflow route (review.md:33, multi-agent.md:187,210). The alternate/downgrade sequential route requires one successful Agent result each and must record a source-attributed downgrade in decisions.md (review.md:57-61, multi-agent.md:187). Config knobs (config.json, state-schema.md:213): stuck_threshold=3, coordinator_lease_s=7200, multi_agent.max_parallel=3, multi_agent.timeout_s=1800, multi_agent.async_timeout_s=3600.
elements.porting_note: Reimplement pm-worker.sh as the Rust dispatch primitive: spawn claude (`claude -p` stream-json) or codex (`codex exec`), enforce timeout, renew lease, and for claude parse the stream-json tool-use trace to assert (a) the orchestration tool (Agent/Workflow) succeeded and (b) the required Skill call (from PM_WORKER_REQUIRED_SKILL, or none if '-') succeeded. Codex/async has NO trace validator — acceptance is repository-evidence only. All timeouts/threshold from config.json defaults above.

invariants: Coordinator NEVER edits implementation files/code locally in any late phase — it only orchestrates, dispatches workers, verifies repository evidence, and writes ledger state (implement.md:9-10; review.md:94; cr.md:76-77).

A worker's success claim / exit code is NEVER proof — acceptance is repository evidence: expected commit/diff exists, changed files within task scope, required tests added+pass, acceptance criteria met (implement.md:92-98; multi-agent.md:326-330).

Task completion is proven only by a completion digest naming (task IDs, commit refs, test/acceptance evidence); a cursor without a digest means RECONCILE (inspect git state), never blind redispatch (implement.md:30-32,127-137; multi-agent.md:339-354).
Never assume a dead/timed-out subprocess made no repository changes — always inspect branches/worktrees before redispatch (implement.md:137).
Exactly ONE branch per slice_id, named pm/slice-<N>-<short-slug>, recorded in every touched package's active_branch; never recreate it with checkout -b (branch-and-cr.md:7-24; implement.md:42-43).

Every external mutation (branch, worktree, task-merge, push, draft-cr, publish, merge/land, comms post) follows pending-before-action → act → complete/fail → reconcile-before-retry using a deterministic state.operations[] key; never infer success from a crashed command (branch-and-cr.md:51-55,88-99; cr.md:129-131).

state.review_state is a single top-level record (slice_id, signature, attempts, updated_at) shared by review AND cr fix loops — exactly one active verification failure at a time; fix loops are serialized even though CR polling may be concurrent (review.md:75-89; cr.md:88-92; branch-and-cr.md:69-71).

attempts key on (slice_id, signature): a different slice_id OR signature resets attempts to 1; the same problem increments; stop when attempts >= config.stuck_threshold (default 3 → 3rd failed fix stops); review_state cleared only on pass or explicit abandon (review.md:84-115).
cr phase NEVER sets phase="done"; only confirming ([A]) — or research re-entry via [B] — reaches done (cr.md:125; confirming.md:12-14).

confirming fire condition is recomputed on EVERY entry (plan tasks exhausted AND crs[] non-empty with all status ∈ {landed,abandoned}); if false, the phase self-corrects back to cr/implement/plan rather than posting (confirming.md:24-46).

Never assume [A] / plan-exhaustion is the coordinator's signal, not the user's; the confirm-done hard stop never auto-resolves on timeout and a file write is never consent (confirming.md:61-63,109-113).

Publish, merge/land, and draft creation are per-review-unit external actions gated by explicit authorization/approval from state-machine.md; publish and merge are two SEPARATE hard stops (cr.md:94-105; branch-and-cr.md:87-99).

Only open review units are polled; a terminal (landed/abandoned) entry clears last_polled to null in the same write and is never polled again (validated by pm-validate.sh) (cr.md:107-110; state-schema.md:187-188).

Independent slices may run concurrently ONLY when their package sets are disjoint (each package has exactly one active_branch); dependent slices stack on the parent branch and rebase after the parent lands (cr.md:119-124; branch-and-cr.md:74-84).

Claude workers must make both the required orchestration call (Agent/Workflow) and the required Skill call (e.g. superpowers:test-driven-development), machine-verified in the trace; codex/async workers have no trace validator and are accepted on repository evidence alone (implement.md:73-90; multi-agent.md:326-330).
gotchas: The pipeline()/parallel()/agent() adversarial-verify block (review.md:37-42) is Claude Workflow-tool DSL pseudocode — do NOT port it literally; the Rust harness fans out N one-shot verifier workers per finding. Only the per-verifier instruction string ('Try to refute: <summary>. Lens: <lens>. Default refuted=true if uncertain.') is borrowed near-verbatim.

Adversarial verify is CONDITIONAL and costly (3× verify tokens): trigger only on risky surface — file paths matching auth/session/token/crypto/payment, DB migrations/schema changes, public-API/irreversible changes (review.md:43-49). Ordinary slices use single-pass verification. Majority-refute drops a finding (>50% of lenses refute).

Two verify fallback layers when the Workflow route is unavailable: (1) sequential read-only Agent calls per lens with a recorded downgrade; (2) capability stop if those are also unavailable (review.md:57-61). Easy to miss when porting the happy path only.

Async worker route is the ONLY path producing run.posture=monitoring and the ONLY sanctioned detached/background execution; it requires Agent:codex + tmux, freezes a deadline independent of the coordinator lease, has NO trace validator, and 'done' always wins races against a dying tmux session (multi-agent.md:268-335). pm-async.sh is pure-decision (no side effects) — keep tmux/state writes in the coordinator.

Operation keys are exact and load-bearing strings; getting them wrong breaks idempotency/dedup: task-worktree:<repo>:<slice_id>:<task_id>, merge-task:<repo>:<slice_id>:<task_id>, branch:<package-or-repo>:<slice_id>, draft-cr:<review-unit>:<slice_id> (review-unit = sorted, URI-escaped package names joined with '+'), push:<repo>:<head-commit> / push:<review-unit>:<commit>, publish:<review-unit>:<revision>, merge:<review-unit>:<revision>, post:<channel>:<content-hash>, async-launch:<task_id> (cr.md:29-30; implement.md:66,102; branch-and-cr.md:36; multi-agent.md:288).
crs[] entry lookup is by (slice_id, package/repo group), NEVER by branch alone — a whole slice shares one branch name across packages/repos, so branch is not a unique key (cr.md:23-24).

A crash-recovery crs[] placeholder may have id:null ONLY while its draft-cr operation is pending; it stays status:"draft", last_polled:null and is not pollable until reconciliation records the remote id (cr.md:40-43).

[B] more-work does NOT overwrite brief.md — it APPENDS a dated 'Addendum (YYYY-MM-DD)' section with the user's reply verbatim, archives plan.md to archive/plan-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md, clears task_cursors to [], and re-enters the FULL research→...→cr pipeline (no shortcut for 'small' asks) (confirming.md:84-99).

Slack-unreachable fallback splits behavior: status UPDATES degrade to STATUS.md, but the BLOCKING confirm-done/publish question PAUSES — a file write is not consent and there is no timeout auto-advance (confirming.md:109-113).

Heavy external-tool coupling in cr.md: cr-babysit skill (Brazil/CRUX analyzers+reviewer polling, `cr --publish`) and gh CLI (`gh pr create --draft --base --head --fill`, `gh pr checks`, `gh pr ready` + reviewer requests), plus git push and `brazil ws sync --md`. The standalone Rust harness must reimplement cr-babysit's polling logic (no runtime skill dependency) and shell out to gh/git/cr.

Downgrades must be recorded as source-attributed decisions.md entries, not silently taken: mixed/all-codex parallel group run sequentially (implement.md:57-60), and the sequential verify fallback (review.md:57-61).

After each material Durable checkpoint the coordinator must rerun pm-due and service newly-due tracks (CRs/stops/async-workers) BEFORE dispatching the next successor — polling cadence is per-item and one due item never advances another's cadence (implement.md:123-124; cr.md:60-62; confirming.md:48-51).

parallel GitHub task merges into the slice branch must be sequential in plan order with a per-merge operation, and the whole group STOPS on the first conflict — do not continue merging siblings (implement.md:100-103).

area: state.json + config.json schemas — the harness's .project-state/ model (references/state-schema.md, state.schema.json, config.schema.json)
overview: .project-state/ is the skill's entire on-disk memory — the only thing surviving context compaction, session handoff, and cold starts. Two machine-authoritative JSON files anchor it: state.json (control state: phase, run posture, cursors, timers, CRs, toolchain, stops, asks, approvals, operations, async workers) validated by state.schema.json, and config.json (intake preferences: comms, CR policy, heartbeat, thresholds, multi-agent knobs) validated by config.schema.json. Both are JSON-Schema draft-2020-12 with strict additionalProperties:false everywhere and heavy conditional (if/then) validation encoding invariants a Rust port must reproduce. There is NO version field — the runtime accepts only the current shape; older ledgers must be backed up and migrated explicitly.

elements.name: .project-state/ directory layout + companion files
elements.detail: Fixed layout (state-schema.md:30-44): state.json (control), .checkpoint.json (state/config/ledger hash seal required before posture changes), config.json, CURRENT.md (always-read entry point), brief.md, design.md, plan.md, decisions.md, progress.md, handoff.md, research/ (one file per topic, raw), archive/ (compacted/pruned detail). Writes batch every non-run field a checkpoint touches through one atomic jq pipeline (scripts/pm-set.sh) under PM_COORDINATOR_RUN_ID=<run-id>, always pretty-printed; run is persisted via pm-harness.sh only after the same lease owner runs pm-checkpoint.sh to seal the validated ledger (state-schema.md:46-56).
elements.porting_note: Model a ProjectState root-dir type. state.json/config.json -> serde structs. The .md files are opaque blobs the harness reads/writes but does not parse (CURRENT.md is a human-readable mirror only). Implement ONE atomic write path (write temp + fsync + rename, serde_json::to_string_pretty) mirroring pm-set.sh; segregate the run field behind a checkpoint-gated writer.

elements.name: phase (state top-level, enum, required)
elements.detail: 9 values in strict order: intake, research, design, plan, implement, review, cr, confirming, done (state.schema.json:23-35; state-schema.md:70). Initial "intake". confirming is the project-boundary hard-stop gate; only user [A] advances confirming->done. Top-level cross-field rule: if run.posture=="done" then phase MUST be "done" (state.schema.json:596-613).
elements.porting_note: enum Phase { Intake, Research, Design, Plan, Implement, Review, Cr, Confirming, Done } with #[serde(rename_all="lowercase")]. Note "cr" lowercases fine but derive rename must map Cr->"cr". Enforce the phase==done <=> posture==done coupling in a validate() method.

elements.name: run (state top-level, object, required) — machine harness posture
elements.detail: Shape {active:bool, posture, owner:string|null, wake_condition:string|null, next_check:int>=0|null, updated_at:int>=0, session_id:string|null, continuations:int>=0, max_continuations:int>=0} (state.schema.json:36-121; state-schema.md:71). posture enum: working|monitoring|needs_you|done. Cold start: {active:false,posture:"working",owner:null,wake_condition:null,next_check:null,updated_at:0,session_id:null,continuations:0,max_continuations:0}. max_continuations:0 means unlimited. Active state is bound to exactly one Claude session (session_id). This is the hook authority; CURRENT.md only mirrors it.
elements.porting_note: Struct Run. Consider modeling posture-dependent nullability with a Rust enum-of-structs (WorkingActive{owner,wake_condition,session_id}, Parked{owner,wake_condition,next_check,session_id}, DoneIdle, Inactive) to make illegal states unrepresentable, OR keep flat with Option<> fields + a validate(). Epochs are i64/u64 seconds. Treat max_continuations==0 as sentinel for unlimited, not zero-budget.

elements.name: run conditional invariants (if/then in schema)
elements.detail: state.schema.json:62-119 encodes: (1) if active==true then owner, wake_condition, session_id must be non-null strings (minLength 1); (2) if active && posture in {monitoring,needs_you} then next_check must be integer>=0 (a real wake epoch); (3) if active && posture==working then next_check MUST be null; (4) if posture==done then active==false AND owner/wake_condition/next_check/session_id all null. Plainly: active parked postures (monitoring/needs_you) require owner + wake condition + next-check epoch; working never has a next_check; done is fully idle.
elements.porting_note: These four if/then blocks are the hardest part to port. Best captured as a Rust enum discriminated by (active, posture). If keeping structs, write a validate_run() returning Result<(),Error> asserting each rule; run it on every load and before every persist. Do NOT let a working posture carry a next_check.

elements.name: task_cursors (state top-level, string[], required, uniqueItems)
elements.detail: Which plan.md tasks are reserved for immediate dispatch OR have returned but are not yet accepted/digested (state-schema.md:72; state.schema.json:122-126). Empty [] before dispatch, at checkpoint edges, and at done. Length 1 = sequential default; length>=2 = one declared 'Parallel with:' group. Review/CR fix loops re-reserve the owning plan task (or reuse its cursor) then dispatch via pm-worker.sh; the coordinator verifies/digests but never edits implementation locally. After interruption, reconcile dispatch checkpoint + task branch + commits + diff + tests before redispatch.
elements.porting_note: Vec<String> of plan task ids; enforce uniqueness (use validation, or a set-like wrapper serializing to array). 'Where is the coordinator working' is DERIVED from task_cursors + plan.md — do NOT add a stored active_package field (state-schema.md:492-495).

elements.name: timers.work (state top-level object, required)
elements.detail: {work: int|null} (state.schema.json:127-134; state-schema.md:73). Last coordinator work-cycle epoch (seconds), null initially. Critical semantic: pm-due.sh returns work:true on EVERY wake regardless of this value — a fresh timestamp is never a reason to skip a work cycle. So it is a record, not a gate.
elements.porting_note: Struct Timers{ work: Option<i64> }. Object wrapper (not a bare scalar) so future timers can be added. Do NOT use it to suppress work cycles.

elements.name: crs[] (state top-level, array, required) — code-review registry
elements.detail: One element per code review (state.schema.json:135-220; state-schema.md:336-381). Fields: id (string|null — CRUX id or GitHub PR number/URL; null ONLY on a non-polled draft-recovery placeholder), slice_id (string, links repo-specific PRs of one logical slice), kind (enum brazil|github, = shared kind of every package the CR spans), branch (string), base (string, branch cut from), status (enum draft|in_review|changes_requested|approved|landed|abandoned), tasks (string[], minItems 1, unique — plan task ids), packages (string[], minItems 1, unique — toolchain.packages[].name), last_polled (int>=0|null), poll_cadence (optional string matching ^[1-9][0-9]*[smhd]$; absent->"20m" default, hot CR "5m", cold "1h").
elements.porting_note: struct Cr { id: Option<String>, slice_id, kind: CrKind, branch, base, status: CrStatus, tasks: Vec<String>, packages: Vec<String>, last_polled: Option<i64>, poll_cadence: Option<Duration> }. enum CrKind{Brazil,Github}; enum CrStatus{Draft,InReview,ChangesRequested,Approved,Landed,Abandoned} rename_all snake_case. 'Open' predicate is load-bearing: status != landed && != abandoned — pm-due.sh uses exactly this; do not rename those two terminal values.

elements.name: crs[] conditional invariants
elements.detail: state.schema.json:191-217: (1) if id==null then status MUST be "draft" AND last_polled MUST be null (identifier-less = recovery-only placeholder; must keep last_polled null and have a matching pending draft-cr:<review-unit>:<slice_id> operation; pm-due.sh excludes it until remote id recorded; review-unit = sorted+URI-escaped packages joined with '+'); (2) if status in {landed,abandoned} then last_polled MUST be null — clear the poll cursor in the SAME write that sets a terminal status, else pm-validate.sh rejects and blocks the checkpoint seal. Only open CRs are polled; each polls independently vs its own poll_cadence (null last_polled counts as due).
elements.porting_note: validate_cr(): assert both implications. When transitioning to Landed/Abandoned, set last_polled=None in the same mutation. Recovery placeholder is a distinct construction path — consider a constructor/type-state so you cannot build an id:None CR with a non-draft status or a poll cursor.

elements.name: toolchain (state top-level, object|null, required) + capabilities
elements.detail: null = detection still owed; non-null = detection complete (state.schema.json:221-302; state-schema.md:75, 123-156). Shape {packages:[...] (minItems 1), capabilities:{...}}. capabilities (all required booleans + detected_at int): detected_at, jq, git, claude, codex, gh, cr_babysit, slack, builder_mcp, tmux. Empty packages:[] only valid at cold-start before Step 2 populates it; non-cold-start empty is a bug.
elements.porting_note: toolchain: Option<Toolchain> where Toolchain{ packages: Vec<Package> (assert non-empty post-detection), capabilities: Capabilities }. struct Capabilities { detected_at: i64, jq: bool, git: bool, claude: bool, codex: bool, gh: bool, cr_babysit: bool, slack: bool, builder_mcp: bool, tmux: bool }. All ten cap fields required — keep exact names (builder_mcp, cr_babysit snake_case).

elements.name: toolchain.packages[] element
elements.detail: One package in scope (state.schema.json:231-276; state-schema.md:455-471). Fields (all required): name (string, Brazil pkg name or github repo name; referenced by crs[].packages), kind (brazil|github), cr (cr-babysit|gh), workspace (string|null — abs Brazil workspace root; required for brazil, null for github; multiple brazil pkgs may share a workspace), path (string — abs pkg root; where verify runs AND worker dispatch cwd so local CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md auto-loads; never derived from workspace+name), verify (string|null — per-pkg build/test cmd, e.g. brazil-build release / npm test / cargo test), active_branch (string|null — current feature branch, null if no slice active; matches newest open CR branch). Conditional (state.schema.json:258-273): if kind==brazil then cr=="cr-babysit" AND workspace is non-null string; else (github) cr=="gh" AND workspace==null.
elements.porting_note: struct Package{ name, kind: PkgKind, cr: CrTool, workspace: Option<String>, path: String, verify: Option<String>, active_branch: Option<String> }. enum CrTool{ #[serde(rename="cr-babysit")] CrBabysit, Gh }. Enforce the kind<->cr<->workspace coupling in validate (or model as enum BrazilPkg{workspace:String,...}/GithubPkg{...}). Package-local agent config (CLAUDE.md/.claude/) is NOT stored — the CLI reads it from cwd (state-schema.md:482-491).

elements.name: open_stops[] element — one unanswered stop question
elements.detail: state.schema.json:303-383; state-schema.md:384-417. Required: id (stable slug; source key for decisions.md), kind (stop kind enum, below), channel (config.comms.channels[].name; defaults to primary), authorized_responders (string[] of authenticated user IDs allowed to resolve/grant; REQUIRED, [] means none yet — replies are feedback but cannot resolve until an authenticated ID recorded), message_id (Slack ts for edit_message; null before first post or for file/terminal), first_posted (int>=0 epoch; anchor for stop_backoff: elapsed_min=(NOW-first_posted)/60), last_polled (int>=0|null), last_seen_reply_ts (Slack ts of highest processed thread reply; init to message_id at first post; poll fetches ts> this, advances cursor to prevent double-processing), status (awaiting_reply|held). Optional: context_ref (string|null — CR id/task id/slug), last_edited (int>=0|null). Conditional (state.schema.json:371-381): if message_id==null then last_seen_reply_ts==null else last_seen_reply_ts is non-null string.
elements.porting_note: struct OpenStop{ id, kind: StopKind, channel: String, context_ref: Option<String>, authorized_responders: Vec<String>, message_id: Option<String>, first_posted: i64, last_polled: Option<i64>, last_seen_reply_ts: Option<String>, last_edited: Option<i64>, status: StopStatus }. enum StopStatus{ AwaitingReply, Held }. Lifecycle: appended on first post; on resolution the element is REMOVED (not marked). Enforce message_id/last_seen_reply_ts null-coupling. [C] hold -> status:held (still polled).

elements.name: open_stops[].kind — the six stop kinds (enum)
elements.detail: publish | confirm_done | ambiguity | stuck | expert_needed | worker_stuck (state.schema.json:322-331; state-schema.md:395). Each value 'determines which playbook owns reply-handling'. publish = per-CR reviewer-visible publish approval; confirm_done = the project-boundary gate (phase confirming); ambiguity = e.g. mixed-kind CR or unclassifiable package; stuck = verification retries exhausted (fires when review_state.attempts >= config.stuck_threshold); expert_needed = pre-contact domain question (becomes an expert_asks[] element after the approved DM); worker_stuck = a blocking worker timed out or a detached async worker was reaped (evidence = its log).
elements.porting_note: enum StopKind{ Publish, ConfirmDone, Ambiguity, Stuck, ExpertNeeded, WorkerStuck } rename_all snake_case. The kind drives a dispatch table to per-phase reply handlers in the harness — keep it a first-class routing key. expert_needed stops migrate to expert_asks[] (see below).

elements.name: expert_asks[] element — one expert-needed ask (DM thread)
elements.detail: state.schema.json:385-455; state-schema.md:420-451. Required: id (slug), question (one-line), channel (config channel name if DM maps to configured channel, else null=ad-hoc), context_ref (task/decision id|null), policy (ask_first|search_first|ask_only — FROZEN copy of config.comms.expert_outreach at ask time so mid-flight config changes can't rewrite history), poc {handle:string, how: user_named|user_authorized_search|search_found_owner, source:string|null (audit trail for search discovery; null when user-named)}, dm_channel (Slack channel id string), thread_ts (DM root msg ts), asked_at (int>=0 epoch), last_polled (int>=0|null), last_seen_reply_ts (string, highest processed DM reply ts; init to thread_ts), status (awaiting_reply|answered|closed). Lifecycle: before contact it is an open_stops[] item with kind:expert_needed; a complete expert_asks[] element is appended ONLY after the approved DM post succeeds (poc/dm_channel/thread_ts/asked_at all known); on reply remove element + record non-trivial answer in decisions.md with expert as Source.
elements.porting_note: struct ExpertAsk{ id, question, channel: Option<String>, context_ref: Option<String>, policy: ExpertOutreach, poc: Poc, dm_channel: String, thread_ts: String, asked_at: i64, last_polled: Option<i64>, last_seen_reply_ts: String, status: ExpertStatus }. struct Poc{ handle: String, how: PocHow, source: Option<String> }. enum PocHow{ UserNamed, UserAuthorizedSearch, SearchFoundOwner }. enum ExpertStatus{ AwaitingReply, Answered, Closed }. Note last_seen_reply_ts here is a plain required String (unlike open_stops where it can be null).

elements.name: expert-DM polling is FIXED (not config)

elements.name: session (state top-level, object|null, required) — heartbeat identity
elements.detail: state.schema.json:457-475; state-schema.md:78. null before heartbeat established. elements.detail: state.schema.json:509-524; state-schema.md:81, 296-310. elements.name: operations (state top-level, array, required) — idempotency journal for external mutations
elements.detail: state.schema.json:525-567; state-schema.md:82, 312-332. Each: id, type (string, e.g. draft_cr), key (string, deterministic+unique for intended effect, e.g. draft-cr:checkout-service:slice-2), status (pending|completed|failed), started_at (int), completed_at (int|null), remote_id (string|null), detail (string|null). elements.name: async_workers[] element — opt-in detached codex worker
elements.detail: state.schema.json:569-594; state-schema.md:83, 499-541. Default blocking worker route NEVER appends here; only a task annotated 'Async: yes' does. elements.name: config: comms.channels[] element

elements.name: config: comms.stop_backoff[] — adaptive cadence for unanswered stops

elements.name: config: comms.expert_outreach (enum)

elements.name: config: cr.publish_approval (const)

elements.name: config: heartbeat / stuck_threshold / coordinator_lease_s
elements.detail: config.schema.json:94-96; state-schema.md:225-227. heartbeat (string ^[1-9][0-9]*[smhd]$, default "15m" — adaptive-cron wake interval). stuck_threshold (int>=1, default 3 — failed fixes allowed INCLUDING the terminal attempt; stop fires when review_state.attempts>=stuck_threshold; default 3 stops after third failed fix). coordinator_lease_s (int>=60, default 7200 — coordinator lease duration; MUST exceed multi_agent.timeout_s by >=60s so a bounded worker terminates before stale takeover; pm-worker.sh renews+verifies the lease immediately before dispatch).

elements.name: config: multi_agent (object)
elements.detail: config.schema.json:97-107; state-schema.md:228-230. Required: max_parallel (int>=1, default 3 — max members in one blocking Workflow fan-out), timeout_s (int>=1, default 1800 — timeout for a blocking direct-CLI worker; a timeout triggers the worker_stuck stop), async_timeout_s (int>=1, default 3600 — wall-clock budget for one detached async worker; frozen into each worker's deadline = started_at+async_timeout_s at launch; independent of coordinator_lease_s and timeout_s, enforced at poll granularity).
