elements.name: Duration string format (shared pattern)
elements.detail: Every cadence/interval field uses regex ^[1-9][0-9]*[smhd]$ — a positive integer followed by unit s|m|h|d (config.schema.json:42,75,94; state.schema.json:189,587). Applies to: heartbeat, comms.channels[].update_cadence, stop_backoff[].poll, crs[].poll_cadence, async_workers[].poll_cadence. No compound ("1h30m") and no zero ("0m") allowed.
elements.porting_note: One shared Duration newtype with FromStr/Display matching the regex exactly (reject leading zero, zero value, compound). Serialize back to the same "<n><unit>" string. Reuse everywhere a cadence appears.

elements.name: CURRENT.md boot-set rule
elements.detail: state-schema.md:544-554. On EVERY entry read exactly the fixed boot set: CURRENT.md, state.json, and the active phase playbook; then read only task-relevant files linked from CURRENT.md or that playbook. On a fresh scaffold CURRENT.md is empty, so state.json selects the intake playbook and nothing else loads. state.run is the hook authority; CURRENT.md merely mirrors its human-readable posture/owner/wake-condition/next-check and is never parsed by hooks.
elements.porting_note: In the Rust harness, the phase playbook text is borrowed verbatim from the copied skill (per-phase files). The boot-set concept becomes: load state.json (authoritative), select the phase playbook prompt by state.phase, regenerate CURRENT.md as a human-readable mirror of run. Do NOT parse CURRENT.md as state input.

invariants: NO version field: runtime accepts ONLY the current shape (state-schema.md:53-56). additionalProperties:false on every object in both schemas — reject unknown keys; use serde deny_unknown_fields.
Cross-object coupling: run.posture=="done" IFF phase=="done" (state.schema.json:596-613 forces phase==done when posture done; state-machine semantics forbid a done posture in any other phase).

run active-state rules: active==true requires non-null owner+wake_condition+session_id; active parked (monitoring/needs_you) requires next_check epoch; active working requires next_check==null; posture done requires active==false and owner/wake_condition/next_check/session_id all null (state.schema.json:62-119).

crs[]: id==null implies status==draft AND last_polled==null (recovery placeholder with a matching pending draft-cr operation); status in {landed,abandoned} implies last_polled==null, cleared in the same write; every CR has >=1 task and >=1 package (minItems 1) (state.schema.json:171-217).
'Open CR' predicate is exactly status!="landed" && status!="abandoned" — pm-due.sh depends on these literal terminal values; do not rename (state-schema.md:356-359).

Package names are unique; every name in crs[].packages resolves in toolchain.packages[]; crs[].kind equals the shared kind of all packages the CR spans; mixed-kind is legal per project but NOT per CR (mixed-kind CR = ambiguity stop) (state-schema.md:178-189, 344-352).

toolchain.packages[]: kind==brazil => cr==cr-babysit AND workspace non-null; kind==github => cr==gh AND workspace==null (state.schema.json:258-273). One github repo per CR element; a brazil CR may span multiple packages in one workspace.

Open CRs for one package form one connected acyclic branch chain; package.active_branch == chain leaf; an ancestor branch can never become active_branch while its child CR is open (state-schema.md:184-186).

Verification retries live ONLY in top-level review_state; there is NO worker-level or CR-level review counter; null review_state means no unresolved verification failure (state-schema.md:84-86, 191-202). Stuck stop fires when review_state.attempts >= config.stuck_threshold.

open_stops[]: message_id==null <=> last_seen_reply_ts==null; authorized_responders is required ([] = no authenticated responder; replies cannot resolve/grant until an authenticated ID is recorded); on resolution the element is REMOVED, not flagged (state.schema.json:371-381; state-schema.md:410-416).

expert_asks[] elements are appended ONLY after the approved DM post succeeds (poc/dm_channel/thread_ts/asked_at all present); before contact the question is an open_stops[] item with kind:expert_needed; policy is a frozen snapshot of config.comms.expert_outreach at ask time (state-schema.md:431, 446-451).

operations[]: key is deterministic + unique per intended effect; persist pending BEFORE acting; a confirmed retry resets the SAME record to pending (never a duplicate key); pending => completed_at/remote_id null; completed => completed_at present (state.schema.json:540-565; state-schema.md:326-332).

async_workers[]: only appended for tasks annotated 'Async: yes'; deadline is FROZEN at launch = started_at + config.multi_agent.async_timeout_s; last_polled is a cursor excluded from checkpoint material_state; only running workers are polled; a past-deadline running worker is reaped to orphaned at poll time (state-schema.md:509-541).

channel_state[] holds runtime timestamps only (config lives in config.json); post-intake, channel_state[].name set must exactly equal the configured channel names, and every Slack target must be non-empty (state-schema.md:288-294).

config: exactly one comms.channels[] element has role==primary (config precedence, not traffic priority); cr.publish_approval is locked to "per_cr"; coordinator_lease_s >= multi_agent.timeout_s + 60 (pm-validate.sh, beyond the JSON schema).

Writes are atomic + pretty-printed via a single jq pipeline (pm-set.sh); the run field is persisted separately (pm-harness.sh) and only after the same lease owner seals a validated ledger via pm-checkpoint.sh; never do incremental multi-pass edits.
pm-due.sh returns work:true on every wake regardless of timers.work; a fresh timestamp is never grounds to skip a work cycle (state-schema.md:73).
'Where is the coordinator working' and package-local agent config are DERIVED / read-from-cwd respectively — never stored in state.json (no active_package field) (state-schema.md:482-495).
gotchas: pm-validate.sh enforces constraints BEYOND the JSON schema (called out via $comment): uniqueness of open_stops/expert_asks/async_workers by id (state.schema.json:306,388,572); open_stops channel references must be configured channels; coordinator_lease_s >= timeout_s+60 (config.schema.json:99). A pure JSON-schema validator is insufficient — port these extra checks too.

The config.comms.channels[].posts enum has FIVE values (status, stops, cr_activity, decisions, expert_dm) but the state-schema.md examples only show three — do not hardcode three (config.schema.json:43-54).

last_seen_reply_ts is nullable on open_stops[] (coupled to message_id) but a REQUIRED non-null string on expert_asks[] (state.schema.json:357-362 vs 451) — different nullability for the same-named field; do not share one type blindly.

Two terminal-value literals are load-bearing for scripts: crs[].status 'landed'/'abandoned' (pm-due.sh open-CR filter) and run.posture 'done'. Renaming any breaks the shell scheduler. Keep serde rename mappings exact.

Several nullable fields are 'oneOf {string,minLength:1} | null' rather than just type:[string,null] — an empty string is INVALID, only a non-empty string or null (e.g. crs[].id, toolchain workspace/verify/active_branch, open_stops message_id). Empty strings must be rejected, not coerced.
run.max_continuations==0 means UNLIMITED, not 'no budget' (state-schema.md:71) — a naive 'continuations < max_continuations' check would immediately halt; special-case 0.

timers is an object {work:int|null} not a bare scalar, and toolchain.capabilities requires all ten boolean/int fields present (missing any fails validation) — keep exact snake_case names builder_mcp, cr_babysit.

crs[].id can be null ONLY for a draft-recovery placeholder that also has status==draft, last_polled==null, and a matching pending 'draft-cr:<review-unit>:<slice_id>' operation where <review-unit> = sorted, URI-escaped package names joined with '+'. This is a subtle cross-array coupling between crs[] and operations[].

deadline enforcement for async workers is by the coordinator at POLL granularity, not a process timeout wrapper — a detached worker outlives the coordinator lease and is only reaped on its next poll; the harness must actively sweep deadlines.

pm-async.sh is pure decision logic: it takes observations (session-alive, done-present) as args, writes no state, and never touches tmux; the coordinator owns all tmux new-session/kill-session and all state writes. Preserve this split when porting (decision fn vs effectful driver).

During intake the scaffold is intentionally partially-invalid (null Slack target, no channel_state entries, empty toolchain.packages); full validation only applies AFTER intake. The port needs a phase-aware validation mode, not one strict schema for all phases.

session.protocol is a const sentinel ('project-manager-heartbeat-v2') proving scheduler ownership; registered_at advances on same-engine re-registration. Even though the Rust harness owns scheduling natively, preserve these fields/const for integrity and interop.
expert-DM poll cadence (1h for 24h then 6h) is hardcoded in pm-due.sh and deliberately NOT a config knob, unlike every other cadence — do not accidentally make it configurable.

last_polled cursors (crs, open_stops, expert_asks, async_workers) are excluded from checkpoint material_state (pm-checkpoint.sh) so a poll-only advance re-seals as no-change; they move monotonically forward and cannot exceed the seal epoch. Material events are launch, status change, and removal.

area: Worker Dispatch + Drive Loop (pm-harness.sh drive-loop actions, pm-worker.sh bounded worker runner, multi-agent.md routing/prompt/async contract)
overview: This slice is the two-layer engine the Rust harness must reimplement: (1) the "drive loop" in pm-harness.sh — a file-locked, lease-guarded posture state machine (`state.json.run`) whose `stop-check` action blocks the coordinator's Stop hook to keep it working across continuations, and whose `wake-check` action coalesces scheduler wakeups against an active run; and (2) the stateless one-shot worker in pm-worker.sh, which builds an exact `claude -p` / `codex exec` invocation, bounds it with GNU `timeout`, captures stdout into a trace file, and (for Claude) validates the stream-json trace proves an ordered TDD-Skill→Agent/Workflow tool-use/result chain. multi-agent.md is the coordinator-side contract: route selection, blocking-surface priority, the 6-part worker prompt template, the opt-in detached async/tmux route, and repository-evidence acceptance. Everything is blocking by default; the parent keeps the scheduler lease while a worker runs.

elements.name: state.json.run object (drive-loop model)
elements.detail: pm-harness.sh:76-136 (run_is_valid) defines the ONLY per-project loop state. Exact key set (no extras, all present): active(bool), posture("working"|"monitoring"|"needs_you"|"done"), owner(null|non-empty str), wake_condition(null|non-empty str), next_check(null|non-neg int epoch), updated_at(non-neg int epoch, required), session_id(null|non-empty str), continuations(non-neg int), max_continuations(non-neg int). Coupling rules: if active → owner+wake_condition+session_id non-empty; posture monitoring/needs_you ⇒ next_check is a number; working ⇒ next_check==null; done+active is invalid. needs_you ⇒ owner must equal an id present in state.open_stops[]. posture done ⇒ active==false and owner/wake_condition/next_check/session_id all null.
elements.porting_note: Model as a Rust enum Posture{Working,Monitoring,NeedsYou,Done} + a Run struct. Port run_is_valid as a validator run on every load AND before every write. Preserve the exact invariant table verbatim; these gates are relied on by hooks that fail-open.

elements.name: stop-check <session-id> (continuation driver — the core loop)
elements.detail: pm-harness.sh:509-583. Called by the coordinator's Stop hook. Returns {active,blocked,resumed,reason,...}. Guards in order: project state invalid→{active:false,...,reason:state_invalid}; run invalid→run_missing_or_invalid; NOT(active && run.session_id==arg && posture==working)→ passes through {active:.run.active,blocked:false,reason:(inactive|session_mismatch|<posture>)}; lease invalid→{active:true,blocked:false,lease_missing_or_expired}; owner.json.session_id empty or != run.session_id→lease_session_mismatch. THEN if max_continuations>0 && continuations>=max → reset run to inactive+working (clears owner/wake/next/session_id) and return reason:max_continuations_reached,blocked:false. ELSE increment run.continuations by 1 (a state mutation) and return {active:true,blocked:true,resumed:false,continuation:N,max_continuations,owner,wake_condition}. blocked:true is what vetoes the Stop and forces the session to keep working.
elements.porting_note: This IS the drive loop. In Rust: while posture==working and lease/session valid and continuations<max, the Stop-equivalent returns blocked/continue and bumps the counter; the coordinator does one pass of real work between continuations. max_continuations==0 means unbounded. The counter increment is a durable side effect — persist under the same lock as the read.

elements.name: wake-check <session-id|-> (scheduler admission / coalescing gate)
elements.detail: pm-harness.sh:391-451. Called by the prompt/scheduler hook to decide whether a heartbeat callback may start a new pass. Returns {admit,coalesced,reason,[owner_run_id,lease_expires_at]}. Fail-OPEN everywhere except one path: run invalid→admit:true run_missing_or_invalid; NOT(active&&working)→ if project state invalid admit:true state_invalid else admit:true reason=(inactive|<posture>); session arg!="-" and !=run.session_id→admit:true session_mismatch; lease invalid→admit:true lease_missing_or_expired; owner session empty/mismatch→admit:true lease_session_mismatch. ONLY when active+working+lease-valid+session-match: admit:false,coalesced:true,reason:active_work with owner_run_id and lease_expires_at (=acquired_at+lease_s). Passing "-" skips the session check.
elements.porting_note: Port the fail-open bias exactly: the sole non-admit case is a live working run under a valid matching lease — everything else admits to avoid deadlocking the loop. This is how a coalesced scheduler callback (fired while a blocking worker held the lease) gets dropped rather than double-driving.

elements.name: start [max-continuations] action
elements.detail: pm-harness.sh:242-291. Requires PM_COORDINATOR_RUN_ID with a valid unexpired lease owned by that run (require_current_lease), and CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID. If a .run exists and is invalid → refuse. MAX = arg else existing max_continuations else 0 (must be non-neg int). Calls ensure_checkpoint_baseline (seals/verifies a baseline via pm-checkpoint.sh) then bind_current_lease_session (writes session_id into owner.json). Idempotent: if already active with same session and posture==working, optionally updates max and re-prints .run. Otherwise writes a fresh run: {active:true,posture:"working",owner:"coordinator",wake_condition:"continue from durable project state",next_check:null,updated_at:now,session_id,continuations:0,max_continuations:MAX}.
elements.porting_note: Borrow the seed run values verbatim (owner="coordinator", wake_condition string). Enforce lease+session preconditions before any activation. Keep idempotency so a re-invoked start doesn't reset continuations.

elements.name: set <posture> <owner|-> <wake|-> [next-check|-] action
elements.detail: pm-harness.sh:293-380. Requires lease + run_is_valid + active + run.session_id==CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID. Posture arg normalizes '-'→'_' (so `needs-you`→needs_you). Rules enforced: non-done requires owner!=- and wake!=-; working requires next==-; monitoring/needs_you require a numeric next-check; needs_you requires owner to match an open_stops[].id; done requires state.phase=="done" and forces owner/wake/next to '-'. MUST pass `pm-checkpoint.sh verify` before writing. Write: posture set, active=(posture!=done), owner/wake/next '-'→null, updated_at=now, session_id=null iff done, continuations reset to 0 unless posture stays working.
elements.porting_note: This is how the coordinator transitions the loop between passes (park to monitoring/needs_you, or finish to done). Port the checkpoint-verify precondition — posture changes are only allowed on a sealed validated ledger. continuations reset-unless-working is subtle: only a working→working set preserves the counter.

elements.name: status / cancel actions
elements.detail: status (382-389): prints .run if valid else {active:false,reason:run_missing_or_invalid}. cancel (485-507): the user's manual escape hatch — DELIBERATELY requires neither lease nor session match (comment 486-491) so a runaway loop whose lease belongs to an unreachable process can still be stopped. Requires run_is_valid, then clears active/owner/wake/next/session_id/continuations but LEAVES posture as-is for diagnosability.
elements.porting_note: Reproduce cancel's no-auth design as a documented escape hatch; do not add lease/session checks or the loop becomes unstoppable until lease expiry. Keep posture untouched on cancel.

elements.name: heartbeat-reconcile action (stdin: CronList JSON array)
elements.detail: pm-harness.sh:453-483. Pure decision, no mutation, no lease required (runs early in bootstrap). Reads config.heartbeat (default "15m"), translates via jq lib scheduling.jq heartbeat_to_cron. Decides from state.session: null→{action:register,cron,reason:null_session}; engine=="loop"→{action:keep,engine:loop}; protocol!="project-manager-heartbeat-v2" or engine!="claude-cron"→{action:replace,stale_job_id,cron}; job_id present in cron_list→{action:keep,job_id}; else→{action:register,reason:missing}.
elements.porting_note: Scheduler-reconciliation logic; the Rust harness owns its own timer so this maps to 'ensure my heartbeat timer matches config'. The protocol sentinel "project-manager-heartbeat-v2" and engine values (claude-cron|loop) live in state.session (state-schema.md:78).

elements.name: Lease + session coupling (require_current_lease / lease_owner_valid / bind_current_lease_session)
elements.detail: pm-harness.sh:147-215. owner.json (in $PS/.coordinator.lock/) holds exactly one record {run_id, acquired_at(int), lease_s(int>0), session_id?}. lease_owner_valid: exactly one object, run_id non-empty (optionally == given run_id), acquired_at/lease_s are non-neg/positive integers, and acquired_at+lease_s>now. require_current_lease demands PM_COORDINATOR_RUN_ID env and that owner.json is a valid unexpired lease owned by it. bind_current_lease_session rewrites owner.json setting session_id (errors if run_id changed). Continuation gates additionally require owner.json.session_id == run.session_id.
elements.porting_note: Port the lease as a small file/record; the Rust harness can keep it in-process but must preserve the (run_id, acquired_at, lease_s, session_id) tuple and the 'lease expires at acquired_at+lease_s' rule. The dual identity check (lease.run_id AND lease.session_id==run.session_id) prevents a stale/other session from driving the loop.

elements.name: Atomic state writes + flock discipline
elements.detail: pm-harness.sh:177-193 rewrite_state: jq into mktemp under $PS, re-validate it is exactly one JSON object, copy perms via `chmod --reference` (fallback stat), then `mv -f`. All actions run under `exec 9<"$PS"; flock -x 9` (233-235) — an exclusive lock on the .project-state directory. NOW is re-read after acquiring the lock unless PM_HARNESS_NOW override set; LEASE_NOW is a fresh `date +%s`.
elements.porting_note: Rust: hold an OS advisory file lock (flock/fcntl) on the state dir for every action; write via temp-file + atomic rename preserving mode. Support a clock override (PM_HARNESS_NOW) for deterministic tests.

elements.name: pm-worker.sh invocation signature + input validation
elements.detail: pm-worker.sh:8 usage: `pm-worker.sh <project-state-dir> <claude|codex> <cwd> <prompt-file> <trace-file> <Agent|Workflow|-> [add-dir ...]`. Requires >=6 args. Validates: PS dir exists, WORKDIR (cwd) exists, PROMPT_FILE exists, TRACE_FILE parent dir exists, jq present, GNU `timeout` present, every add-dir is an existing dir. Reads full prompt text via `PROMPT="$(<PROMPT_FILE)"`. Env: PM_WORKER_REQUIRED_SKILL (default "superpowers:test-driven-development", set "-" for read-only; must be non-empty), PM_WORKER_KILL_AFTER_S (default 30, must be int 1..30), PM_COORDINATOR_RUN_ID (required when state active/leased).
elements.porting_note: This is the exact stateless-worker contract the Rust harness must expose: (state-dir, worker-kind, cwd, prompt-text/file, trace-path, expected-orchestration-tool, add-dirs[]). The prompt is read from a file and passed as one argv token — not stdin. add-dirs beyond cwd map to extra --add-dir args.

elements.name: Claude command construction (exact flags)
elements.detail: pm-worker.sh:81-102. EXPECTED_TOOL must be Agent or Workflow (else usage/exit 1). PERMISSION_MODE="plan" iff REQUIRED_SKILL=="-" (read-only), else "acceptEdits". COMMAND = `env -u CLAUDECODE claude -p --permission-mode <mode> --no-session-persistence --output-format stream-json --verbose --forward-subagent-text` then one `--add-dir <dir>` per add-dir, then `-- "$PROMPT"`.
elements.porting_note: Borrow these flags VERBATIM. `env -u CLAUDECODE` strips the parent marker so the nested claude runs as a fresh CLI (critical). --output-format stream-json --verbose is required so the trace validator can see tool-use/result records. Prompt is the final argv after `--`.

elements.name: Codex command construction (exact flags)
elements.detail: pm-worker.sh:103-112. EXPECTED_TOOL must be "-" (else usage). COMMAND = `codex -a never -s workspace-write exec --ephemeral` then one `--add-dir <dir>` per add-dir, then `-- "$PROMPT"`. No Skill/trace requirement for codex.
elements.porting_note: Borrow verbatim. `-a never` = never ask for approval; `-s workspace-write` = sandbox write scope; `exec --ephemeral` = one-shot no-persistence. Codex trace is raw stdout, NOT stream-json — no proof validation runs.

elements.name: Timeout / kill bounding + output capture
elements.detail: pm-worker.sh:120-139. TIMEOUT_S read from config.multi_agent.timeout_s (must be int>=1; default 1800). Runs `( cd "$WORKDIR"; exec timeout --kill-after="${KILL_AFTER_S}s" "${TIMEOUT_S}s" "${COMMAND[@]}" ) > "$TRACE_FILE"` — worker STDOUT is redirected to the trace file; stderr is inherited. RC handling: 0→continue; 124 or 137→print `<worker> timed out after <T>s`, exit 124; any other RC→print `<worker> exited with status <RC>; trace preserved at <file>`, exit that RC.
elements.porting_note: Rust: spawn the child in its own process group in WORKDIR, enforce a wall-clock timeout, then SIGTERM and after kill-after grace SIGKILL the whole group. Treat 124/137 as timeout. Always capture stdout to the trace path and preserve it on any failure. The timeout MUST be shorter than the coordinator lease (see renew element).

elements.name: Claude stream-json trace proof validation
elements.detail: pm-worker.sh:141-225. jq -s slurps the trace as an array of complete records. Extracts tool_uses (assistant records with array content → type==tool_use) tagged with record_index, and tool_results (records with array content → type==tool_result). named($req): tool name == $req OR name endswith "__"+$req (handles MCP-prefixed names). has_successful_result: use.tool.id is non-empty string AND some tool_result has tool_use_id==id, is_error!=true, record_index>use.record_index, and (before==null or <before). orchestration = first successful EXPECTED_TOOL use, else first such use, else null. skill_uses = Skill uses whose input.skill==REQUIRED_SKILL; ordered_skill_uses = those with record_index < orchestration.record_index; successful_skill_uses = those with a successful result before orchestration. Missing-proof messages joined by " and ": no orchestration use→"<T> tool-use event"; uses but none successful→"successful tool result for <T>"; (skill, only if REQUIRED!="-") no skill use→"Skill tool-use event for <skill>"; skill exists but none before orchestration→"...in an earlier assistant turn than <T>"; ordered but none successful→"successful tool result for <skill> before <T>". jq parse failure→exit 3 'not valid stream-json'; non-empty missing-proof→exit 3 'lacks required <...>'.
elements.porting_note: Port this verbatim as the acceptance gate for Claude implementation/read-only calls. Key rules to preserve: (a) match tool_use↔tool_result by id; (b) require the TDD Skill in a STRICTLY EARLIER assistant record than the orchestration (proves the envelope could read the Skill result before delegating); (c) endswith("__"+name) namespacing match; (d) only complete records count — ignore partial stream deltas. Exit 3 is the distinct 'proof failed' code.

elements.name: renew_dispatch_lease (pre-dispatch lease renewal)
elements.detail: pm-worker.sh:47-73, called at :118 right before spawning. If .coordinator.lock dir absent AND state.run.active!=true → no lease needed (return 0). Otherwise: require PM_COORDINATOR_RUN_ID; read config.coordinator_lease_s (int>=1); FAIL unless lease_s >= TIMEOUT_S+60; call `pm-lock.sh renew <PS> <run_id> <lease_s>` which fails if the lease is missing/expired/owned by another run.
elements.porting_note: Reimplement: immediately before launching each worker, renew the coordinator's lease so the worker's hard timeout is guaranteed to fire before any stale-takeover window. Enforce coordinator_lease_s >= timeout_s+60. When no run is active and no lock exists, dispatch may proceed unleased (e.g., standalone tooling).

elements.name: Worker output contract (what the caller consumes)
elements.detail: pm-worker.sh:227-231 success: prints compact JSON `{ok:true,worker:<claude|codex>,expected_tool:<T>,trace:<path>}` on stdout, exit 0. The trace file holds the worker's full stdout (stream-json for claude, raw for codex). Failure surfaces: exit 124 (timeout), exit 3 (claude trace invalid or missing required proof), or the worker's own non-zero exit code, each with a stderr diagnostic; trace is always preserved.
elements.porting_note: The Rust dispatch fn returns Ok(WorkerResult{worker,expected_tool,trace_path}) on 0, and typed errors Timeout / ProofFailed / WorkerExit(code) otherwise. Downstream, a success verdict is NOT task acceptance — repository evidence gates that (see acceptance element).

elements.name: Route selection / blocking-surface priority
elements.detail: multi-agent.md:48-66 & 160-172. Use first valid route: (1) all-Claude `Parallel with:` group → one hard-timed claude -p envelope instructed to make a dynamic `Workflow parallel()` with one `agent()` per member; (2) sequential Claude task → one claude -p envelope requiring one fresh `Agent` call; (3) Codex task → one `codex exec`; (4) mixed/all-Codex parallel group → run members sequentially through their bounded route and log the downgrade in decisions.md; (5) if required CLI or hard `timeout` unavailable → raise a capability stop (never implement inline). max_parallel (config.multi_agent.max_parallel, default 3) caps a Workflow group and MUST be enforced by the coordinator before dispatch — pm-worker.sh cannot infer fan-out.
elements.porting_note: Port as the dispatcher's route() function. Borrow the pseudocode at :160-172 verbatim as the spec. The Rust coordinator must cap the parallel member list to max_parallel before building the Workflow prompt, and record any sequential downgrade with a sourced decisions.md entry.

elements.name: Worker prompt contract (6 mandatory sections)
elements.detail: multi-agent.md:242-264. Every worker prompt contains: 1) goal, hard constraints, task acceptance criteria, package+branch context, binding decisions from handoff.md; 2) links to relevant plan/design/research files; 3) (Claude only) instruction to invoke superpowers:test-driven-development via the Skill tool before editing — trace must contain that exact Skill id in input.skill; 4) the required orchestration action (one Agent for sequential, one dynamic Workflow for an all-Claude parallel group); 5) a prelude-read list of every existing file the worker may modify; 6) a final response contract: changed files, commit ref, tests run+results, remaining risks, explicit failure/blocker when incomplete. Paths kept relative to worker cwd/worktree. FORBID background jobs/detached processes/setsid/nohup/daemonization/long-lived services (async route is the only exception, owned by the coordinator via tmux).
elements.porting_note: Borrow this 6-item structure as the Rust prompt template (adapt wording, keep the exact Skill id string and the ordered Skill→orchestration requirement so the trace validator passes). The parallel target JS at multi-agent.md:195-200 (`await parallel(tasks.map(...agent(renderWorkerPrompt(task),{label})))`) should be embedded verbatim in the parallel prompt.

elements.name: Task annotations (plan.md routing metadata)
elements.detail: multi-agent.md:71-129. Annotations that change the default (one Claude subagent, bounded envelope from project root): `Agent:` claude(default)|codex; `Isolate: yes` (dedicated checkout); `Parallel with:` (independent siblings); `Package:` (names toolchain.packages[]; first is worker cwd, rest go in prompt or as --add-dir); `Async: yes` (detached codex route, requires Agent:codex + tmux). Isolation by package kind: github→per-task branch+worktree off the slice branch; brazil→existing package checkout on slice branch, NEVER a separate worktree (brazil-build resolves via <workspace>/src/<Package>). Parallel GitHub tasks always use separate branches/worktrees and merge into slice branch one at a time in plan order. Reject invalid annotations (overlapping files, shared Brazil package, codex on exploratory task, unresolvable Package) with a sourced decisions.md correction; raise an ambiguity stop only if no safe correction.
elements.porting_note: Port as a parsed PlanTaskAnnotations struct feeding route(). The github-vs-brazil isolation rule directly determines the worker `cwd` and add-dirs passed to pm-worker.sh, and whether two tasks may run concurrently. Encode the reject/downgrade rules as validation.

elements.name: Async worker route (opt-in detached tmux/codex)
elements.detail: multi-agent.md:268-335. Only route producing `monitoring` posture; registry is state.async_workers[]. `pm-async.sh` ONLY decides, never touches tmux/fs/state: `pm-async.sh <ps> poll <id> <session-alive 0|1> <done-present 0|1> <now>` → verdict. Coordinator does all tmux (new-session -d -s pm-aw-<id> running codex wrapped to write exit code to done_signal file and pipe stdout/stderr to log; has-session; kill-session) and all state writes/checkpoints. Launch: persist pending async-launch:<task_id>, start tmux, complete op, append async_workers[] with deadline=started_at+config.multi_agent.async_timeout_s (frozen, independent of lease), close MATERIAL checkpoint. Park: set run monitoring (owner=worker id, next_check=poll cadence), release lease. Poll verdicts: running→advance last_polled only (re-seal no-change); done→read exit code+log then VERIFY branch/diff/tests exactly as a blocking return, on accept write digest+kill-session+remove element+material checkpoint; orphaned(session_gone|deadline_exceeded)→kill-session, set element status:orphaned, raise worker_stuck with log. done always wins races.
elements.porting_note: Port pm-async.sh as a pure decision fn (record + 2 observations + now → verdict) and keep all effects (tmux, state, checkpoints) in the coordinator. deadline is frozen at launch and enforced at poll granularity, NOT by a timeout wrapper. An exit code of 0 does NOT accept the task — repository evidence does (no stream-json validator on this path).

elements.name: Recovery after interruption + worker_stuck stop
elements.detail: multi-agent.md:339-377. A task cursor written before dispatch but lacking a completion digest means RECONCILE, not auto-redispatch: inspect task branch/worktree+slice branch, compare commits/files vs acceptance criteria, run/verify acceptance tests; if complete merge+write digest; if partial preserve useful commits and dispatch only missing criteria to a fresh blocking worker; if nothing trustworthy, retry whole task. Raise open_stops[].kind:"worker_stuck" when a worker call fails/times out, its return lacks verification evidence, repo state conflicts with the claim, or expected commit/diff/tests can't be reconciled. Offer options [A] retry missing work fresh / [B] retry via alternate blocking surface / [C] show captured result+evidence / [D] skip or block (D needs a sourced decisions.md entry). Preserve captured output+partial commits until resolved.
elements.porting_note: Port the task-cursor-before-dispatch ordering as the crash-recovery handle. The Rust harness must implement the reconcile ladder and the worker_stuck stop kind with those four options; timeouts/exit!=0/proof-failure from pm-worker all funnel into worker_stuck.

elements.name: Config keys consumed by dispatch (defaults)
elements.detail: From pm-init.sh:127-130 / state-schema.md:225-230: heartbeat "15m"; coordinator_lease_s 7200; multi_agent.max_parallel 3; multi_agent.timeout_s 1800 (blocking worker timeout → worker_stuck on timeout); multi_agent.async_timeout_s 3600 (frozen per-worker deadline). Constraint: coordinator_lease_s must exceed multi_agent.timeout_s by >=60s (enforced by pm-worker renew_dispatch_lease).
elements.porting_note: Represent as a Config struct with these defaults; validate coordinator_lease_s >= timeout_s+60 at load. These are the only config values the dispatch/loop path reads.

invariants: state.json must always be exactly one JSON object; every mutation validates this before and after (rewrite_state re-checks the temp file) and all actions run under an exclusive flock on the .project-state dir.
State writes are atomic: jq→mktemp under the state dir→re-validate→preserve mode via chmod --reference→mv -f. Never write in place.

Coordinator mutations (start/set) require PM_COORDINATOR_RUN_ID owning a valid, unexpired lease AND CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID matching run.session_id; continuation gates (stop-check/wake-check) additionally require owner.json.session_id == run.session_id. cancel is the ONLY mutation that intentionally skips both checks (escape hatch).

The drive loop runs only while posture==working: stop-check returns blocked:true (continue) and increments continuations until continuations>=max_continuations (max>0) or posture leaves working; max_continuations==0 is unbounded.

wake-check fails OPEN in every case except a live working run under a valid matching lease+session, which returns admit:false/coalesced:true — this coalesces scheduler callbacks fired while a blocking worker held the lease and prevents double-driving.

Every bounded worker is blocking by default and hard-timed via GNU timeout with a kill-after grace; the worker's timeout must be strictly shorter than the coordinator lease, and the lease is renewed immediately before each dispatch.
The parent coordinator remains the scheduler/lease owner while pm-worker.sh blocks; neither the Claude child nor codex exec inherits the parent's scheduled callback.

Claude implementation traces must prove an ordered chain: a successful superpowers:test-driven-development Skill tool-use/result in a STRICTLY EARLIER assistant record than a successful Agent/Workflow tool-use/result, matched by tool_use_id. Read-only envelopes (PM_WORKER_REQUIRED_SKILL=-) drop the Skill requirement and use permission-mode plan.

A worker's success claim (JSON verdict, exit 0, or async exit code 0) is never task acceptance; acceptance requires verifying branch state, diff scope, and acceptance tests against the repository — identically for blocking and async returns.
posture==done requires state.phase=="done", clears the run's activation fields, and is the only terminal posture; posture set to done deactivates the run.
needs_you posture is only valid when its owner equals an id in state.open_stops[]; parked postures (monitoring/needs_you) require a numeric next_check while working requires next_check==null.

Never place concurrent workers on the same checkout; parallel GitHub tasks use private task branches/worktrees merged into the slice branch one-at-a-time in plan order; Brazil tasks sharing a package run sequentially on the slice branch (external worktree breaks brazil-build resolution).
Worker prompts forbid background jobs/detached processes/daemonization; the opt-in async/tmux route is the sole exception and its detachment is owned by the coordinator, not the worker prompt.
A required CLI (claude/codex) or GNU timeout being unavailable raises a capability stop; the coordinator must never implement a task inline.
gotchas: Tool-name matching in the trace validator uses `name == required OR name endswith "__"+required` — this exists to match MCP-namespaced names (e.g. mcp__plugin__Agent). The Rust validator must replicate the endswith rule or valid traces will be rejected.

The trace is slurped as an array of COMPLETE stream-json records (jq -s); partial stream deltas are ignored. Only fully-formed assistant records with array content contribute tool_use/tool_result events.

Exit-code semantics are load-bearing: 0=success (prints {ok:true} JSON), 124=timeout (also mapped from raw 137/SIGKILL), 3=Claude trace invalid or missing required proof, any other=the worker's own exit code. The trace file is preserved on every failure.
pm-worker enforces worker/expected-tool pairing: claude REQUIRES EXPECTED_TOOL in {Agent,Workflow}; codex REQUIRES EXPECTED_TOOL == "-". A mismatch is a usage error (exit 1), not a proof failure.

`env -u CLAUDECODE` before the nested `claude -p` is essential — without unsetting the parent's CLAUDECODE marker the nested CLI misbehaves. Only unset it at the Claude boundary; do not strip it globally.

stop-check mutates state as a side effect (continuations += 1, or a full reset on max reached). The 'drive loop counter' lives inside what looks like a read-only hook check — persist it under the same lock as the read.

The prompt is read from a file and passed as a single argv token after `--`, never via stdin. Very large prompts hit argv limits; the Rust harness should keep prompts file-backed and be mindful of ARG_MAX.

config.multi_agent.timeout_s is read by pm-worker but the coordinator_lease_s>=timeout_s+60 invariant is only checked inside renew_dispatch_lease and only when state is active/leased — an unleased dispatch skips lease renewal entirely (lock dir absent AND run inactive).

pm-worker.sh cannot enforce max_parallel or verify Workflow internals (real concurrency, one agent() per member, dynamic script construction) — the trace only proves a Workflow tool-use/result pair ran. The coordinator MUST cap the member list before building the prompt; this is a prompt/coordinator responsibility the runner cannot back-stop.

The async route has NO stream-json trace validator (it can't watch a detached worker's tool calls); it relies entirely on repository-evidence acceptance and a frozen deadline. An exit code of 0 written to done_signal does not accept the task.

Async deadline is frozen at launch (started_at + async_timeout_s) and is INDEPENDENT of the coordinator lease and the blocking timeout — enforced only at poll granularity, so a detached worker can outlive several coordinator entries but is reaped to orphaned on the first poll at/after deadline.

Dependencies outside this slice that the port must also provide or stub: pm-lock.sh (lease acquire/renew/release; owner.json shape {run_id,acquired_at,lease_s,session_id?}), pm-checkpoint.sh (baseline seal + verify gating start/set), pm-validate.sh (project_state_is_valid), pm-due.sh (produces due tracks + due_async_workers after each dispatch), pm-async.sh (pure poll-verdict fn), and lib/scheduling.jq (heartbeat_to_cron). The drive loop and dispatch call these but they belong to other slices.

heartbeat-reconcile and wake-check are deliberately lease-free and side-effect-free so they can run early in bootstrap and from hooks; do not add lease requirements when porting or bootstrap deadlocks.

After each dispatch+checkpoint the coordinator must run pm-due.sh to pick up scheduler callbacks that coalesced (via wake-check) while the blocking worker held the lease (multi-agent.md:153-156) — the drive loop's 'catch up on missed wakeups' step.

area: Integrity (checkpoint sealing + state validation), Coordinator lease/lock, Autonomy-tier/stop model, and Stops/Comms semantics — from pm-checkpoint.sh, pm-validate.sh, pm-lock.sh, principles.md, comms.md (plus load-bearing lib/scheduling.jq and pm-due.sh).
overview: These files are the integrity + control-plane substrate the harness must own in Rust. pm-validate.sh is the authoritative schema/invariant checker for the ledger (state.json + config.json); pm-checkpoint.sh seals cryptographic snapshots of the ledger so a validated state cannot be silently mutated and so monotonic progress (poll cursors, journal ops, comms posts) is enforced; pm-lock.sh implements a single-writer coordinator lease. principles.md defines the "max autonomy" model where phase gates auto-waive but three principle-derived stops always halt the loop, and comms.md defines how those stops/questions are raised, routed, polled, and resolved through configured channels. The whole thing runs at ONE autonomy tier (max): phases auto-flow; only stops and approval gates interrupt.

elements.name: Checkpoint kinds (4) and what each seals
elements.detail: pm-checkpoint.sh usage (lines 6-13): `seal <id> <baseline|material|no-change|journal>`, `check-seal`, `verify`. baseline = first-ever seal (only allowed when no stamp exists, line 517-521). material = a real workflow advance; REQUIRES CURRENT.md/handoff.md/progress.md non-empty AND (if a prior stamp exists) each of those 3 narrative files' hash MUST differ from the sealed hash (lines 522-537). journal = bookkeeping-only advance (heartbeat/post ops, channel last_posted, session): journal_guard hash MUST be unchanged and config.json+CURRENT.md+handoff.md+progress.md+decisions.md files MUST be byte-identical to the seal (lines 538-559). no-change = a monitoring wake with nothing material: material_state hash MUST be unchanged and the same 5 files unchanged (lines 560-577). Note both journal and no-change permit state.json to change (only its polling/bookkeeping cursors).
elements.porting_note: Model as `enum CheckpointKind { Baseline, Material, NoChange, Journal }`. Each kind is a distinct set of preconditions over the ledger snapshot; encode as a match arm returning Result<(), SealError>. Borrow the exact error strings for parity with existing tests.

elements.name: Snapshot structure (the sealed .checkpoint.json)
elements.detail: snapshot() (lines 159-187) writes {files:{6 sha256 hashes of state.json,config.json,CURRENT.md,handoff.md,progress.md,decisions.md}, control_state, material_state, journal_guard, journal, bookkeeping}. Stamp path is `$ROOT/.project-state/.checkpoint.json` (line 22). The 6 ledger files are the FILES array (line 26).
elements.porting_note: Struct `Checkpoint { id:String, kind:CheckpointKind, sealed_at:i64, control_state:Hex64, material_state:Hex64, journal_guard:Hex64, journal:JournalBookkeeping, bookkeeping:PollBookkeeping, files:BTreeMap<String,Hex64> }`. Serialize with sorted keys (jq -cS) so hashes are reproducible. Use sha256.

elements.name: Three canonicalized state hashes: control_state / material_state / journal_guard
elements.detail: control_state_hash = sha256 of `del(.run)` of state.json (lines 155-157) — everything except the ephemeral run block. material_state_hash = del(.run) + null out .timers.work + null last_polled on crs/open_stops/expert_asks/async_workers (lines 66-75) — the durable workflow state ignoring poll cursors. journal_guard_hash = del(.run,.session) + null timers.work + null the 4 last_polled cursors + null channel_state[].last_posted + DROP operations of type heartbeat/post (lines 77-94) — i.e. everything EXCEPT bookkeeping/journal/session. These are computed over canonical (sorted-key, compact) JSON.
elements.porting_note: Implement three canonicalizer functions that take serde_json::Value, apply the deletions/nullings, then hash the canonical serialization. journal_guard changing ⇒ real workflow change (rejects a journal checkpoint). material_state changing ⇒ material change (rejects a no-change checkpoint). control_state is what `verify` compares.

elements.name: journal bookkeeping vs poll bookkeeping payloads
elements.detail: journal_bookkeeping (lines 96-120) = {session, channels:[{name,last_posted} sorted by name], operations:[heartbeat|post ops as {id,type,key,status,started_at,completed_at,remote_id,detail} sorted by key]}. poll_bookkeeping (lines 122-153) = {work:.timers.work, crs:[{id, review_unit(=sorted uri-encoded packages joined '+' then ':'+slice_id), last_polled, terminal(=status landed|abandoned)} sorted by review_unit,id], open_stops/expert_asks/async_workers:[{key:id,last_polled} sorted by key]}.
elements.porting_note: review_unit key derivation (packages sorted, %-encoded, joined with '+', then ':'+slice_id) appears in BOTH pm-checkpoint and pm-validate — make it ONE shared Rust fn (DRY). terminal CR ⇒ last_polled must be null.

elements.name: Seal preconditions (order matters)
elements.detail: On `seal` (lines 463-515): (1) validate id non-empty and kind in set; (2) IF `.coordinator.lock` dir exists OR state.json `.run.active==true`, require env PM_COORDINATOR_RUN_ID and call pm-lock assert-held to prove the caller owns the unexpired lease (lines 475-489); (3) run pm-validate.sh — MUST pass (line 490); (4) build snapshot; (5) every poll bookkeeping cursor (work + all last_polled) MUST be null or <= NOW (lines 492-505); (6) if a stamp exists and kind!=baseline: stamp_is_valid AND bookkeeping_moves_forward (lines 506-515); (7) per-kind checks; (8) atomic write via mktemp+`mv -f` (lines 580-597). NOW comes from `date +%s` (or PM_CHECKPOINT_NOW override for tests).
elements.porting_note: Seal = validate-then-snapshot-then-monotonicity-then-kind-rules-then-atomic-write. The lease assertion couples checkpoint to lock: only the lease owner may seal while active. Preserve this exact ordering; monotonicity must be checked BEFORE writing.

elements.name: check-seal and verify actions
elements.detail: check-seal (lines 450-461): stamp must exist and be structurally valid (stamp_is_valid); prints it. verify (lines 601-626): stamp exists+valid, then recompute snapshot and assert files (EXCLUDING state.json) all equal, control_state equal, material_state equal, journal_guard equal, journal equal (lines 612-621). Note verify does NOT compare state.json's file hash and does NOT compare bookkeeping — because poll cursors legitimately advance between seal and verify. verify's guarantee: the durable ledger content has not changed since the seal.
elements.porting_note: verify is the read-side integrity check the harness runs before trusting a resumed ledger. Implement as: recompute canonical hashes, compare the durable subset. Deliberately skip state.json raw-file hash + bookkeeping.

elements.name: stamp_is_valid — structural schema of the seal
elements.detail: Lines 189-274. id non-empty string; kind in {baseline,material,no-change,journal}; sealed_at int>=0; control_state/material_state/journal_guard each match ^[0-9a-f]{64}$; files object has EXACTLY keys [CURRENT.md,config.json,decisions.md,handoff.md,progress.md,state.json] all 64-hex; bookkeeping has EXACTLY keys [async_workers,crs,expert_asks,open_stops,work] with typed cursors (cursor = null or non-negative integer; keyed_cursors require unique non-empty string keys; cr_cursors require unique review_unit + unique non-null ids + terminal boolean); journal matches journal_bookkeeping schema (session null or the cron-loop object; channels/operations typed with the exact operation key set and status/type enums).
elements.porting_note: This is the deserialization contract for a persisted checkpoint. In Rust, strict structs + serde `deny_unknown_fields` give you keys_exact for free; enforce the hex64 regex and cursor invariants in a validate() method.

elements.name: journal_moves_forward — monotonic bookkeeping transitions
elements.detail: Lines 276-388. session may only: stay equal; go null→set (with registered_at a valid int <=now AND a completed heartbeat op whose remote_id==job_id); or rotate (job_id changes, registered_at strictly increases <=now, same kind/protocol/engine, matching completed heartbeat). Channels: count unchanged, every after-channel existed before, last_posted monotonic non-decreasing and <=now. Operations: every BEFORE op must still exist (by key) and satisfy operation_moves_forward = identity(id,type,key) unchanged AND one of {unchanged | pending→completed/failed (started_at fixed, completed_at valid & in [started_at,now]) | failed→pending retry (started_at strictly increases <=now, completed_at & remote_id null) | failed→completed (started_at fixed)}. Every AFTER op either existed before or is a brand-new pending op (started_at<=now, no completion fields).
elements.porting_note: This is a state-machine on external-operation records: pending→{completed,failed}, failed→{pending(retry, new started_at),completed}. Encode as a transition validator. The retry path bumping started_at is how idempotent retries are audited. Critical for the 'external actions explicit and idempotent' invariant.

elements.name: bookkeeping_moves_forward — monotonic poll cursors
elements.detail: Lines 390-436. cursor_forward(before,after): if before null then after is null or (int, >=0, <=now); else after is int >= before and <= now. Applied to work timer, and to crs (matched by id OR review_unit, at most one match; a terminal CR may reset last_polled to null), open_stops/expert_asks/async_workers (matched by key). Guarantees poll cursors never move backward and never exceed seal time.
elements.porting_note: Poll cursors are monotonic clocks. When porting, a CR that became terminal is allowed to null its cursor (exception to monotonicity). Match CRs by id first, else review_unit.

elements.name: Checkpoint concurrency guard (flock)
elements.detail: Lines 438-442: unless PM_CHECKPOINT_LOCK_HELD=1, the script require_files then `exec 9<"$PS"; flock -x 9` — an exclusive advisory lock on the .project-state directory FD, held for the whole operation. jq and flock are hard requirements (lines 28-39). NOW is re-read after acquiring the lock (lines 443-445).
elements.porting_note: Serialize all ledger mutations (seal + lock transitions) under one exclusive OS lock on the project-state dir. In Rust use flock(2)/fcntl or a file lock crate; keep the PM_CHECKPOINT_LOCK_HELD reentrancy flag concept so a caller already holding the lock (e.g. seal calling pm-lock assert-held) does not deadlock.

elements.name: Coordinator lease/lock — atomic-directory design
elements.detail: pm-lock.sh. The lease is a directory `$PS/.coordinator.lock` containing owner.json {run_id, acquired_at, lease_s, [session_id]}. Actions: acquire (line 91): `mkdir` the dir atomically; on success write owner (now=date), return {acquired:true,expires_at:now+lease,stale_takeover:false}; if dir exists, read owner (fallback to dir mtime+lease if owner.json unparseable) and if now<acquired_at+lease_s return busy(exit 2), else STALE TAKEOVER: mv lock aside, mkdir fresh, write owner, rm aside, return stale_takeover:true+previous_run_id. renew (line 193): owner.json must be owned by run_id AND unexpired, else exit 2 not_owner_or_expired; rewrites acquired_at=now preserving session_id. release (line 161): dir must exist (else not_locked exit 2) and owner run_id must match (else not_owner exit 2). assert-held (line 41): read-only; held iff owner run_id matches, acquired_at/lease_s valid ints, and acquired_at+lease_s>now (exit 0), else exit 2 with owner_run_id+expires_at.
elements.porting_note: Reimplement lease as: atomic dir create = compare-and-swap; owner.json = lease metadata. Exit codes: 0 success, 2 contention/not-owner/expired, 1 usage/error — preserve for callers. Lease seconds must be a positive integer; config.coordinator_lease_s>=60 and >= multi_agent.timeout_s+60 (enforced in pm-validate).

elements.name: Lock serialization + reentrancy
elements.detail: serialize_transitions() (lines 31-37) takes `flock -x 9` on the PS dir before any acquire/renew/release/assert-held mutation. assert-held skips flock when PM_COORDINATOR_LOCK_HELD=1 (line 50) — used when pm-checkpoint already holds the flock and asserts ownership inline (pm-checkpoint line 483 sets PM_COORDINATOR_LOCK_HELD=1). Writes are atomic via tmp file + `mv` (write_owner, lines 13-29).
elements.porting_note: Same single OS lock on the project-state dir guards BOTH checkpoint seals and lock transitions — they cannot run concurrently. Keep the reentrancy env-flag pattern (or pass a 'lock already held' bool).

elements.name: state.json top-level schema (pm-validate)
elements.detail: pm-validate.sh lines 130-131: state keys EXACTLY [phase, run, task_cursors, timers, crs, toolchain, open_stops, expert_asks, session, review_state, channel_state, approvals, operations, async_workers]. phase in {intake,research,design,plan,implement,review,cr,confirming,done} (line 135). task_cursors = array of unique strings. timers = {work: int|null} only. Output is {valid:bool, errors:[string]}; exits non-zero if invalid (lines 519-526).
elements.porting_note: Strict struct with deny_unknown_fields. phase is the 9-state machine enum the harness owns. Return a structured {valid, errors[]} so callers can surface the exact error strings (borrow them verbatim).

elements.name: state.run object — posture invariants
elements.detail: Lines 137-172 + cross-checks 513-518. run keys EXACTLY & all required: [active(bool), posture, owner, wake_condition, next_check, updated_at, session_id, continuations, max_continuations]. posture in {working,monitoring,needs_you,done}. owner/wake_condition/session_id: null or non-empty string. next_check int|null. updated_at int>=0. continuations & max_continuations int>=0. IF active: owner+wake_condition+session_id must be non-empty; posture monitoring|needs_you ⇒ next_check int>=0; posture working ⇒ next_check==null. posture done ⇒ active==false and owner/wake_condition/next_check/session_id all null AND state.phase==done. posture needs_you (while active) ⇒ some open_stops[].id == run.owner.
elements.porting_note: This is the core scheduler posture machine. Encode as an enum RunPosture with a validate(run, phase, open_stops) that enforces the conditional field requirements. 'needs_you must point at a real open stop' and 'done requires phase==done' are cross-object invariants.

elements.name: state.crs — CR records + branch-chain invariant
elements.detail: Lines 181-305. Each CR: keys exactly [id,slice_id,kind,branch,base,status,tasks,packages,last_polled,poll_cadence(optional)]. id null-or-nonempty; kind in {brazil,github}; status in {draft,in_review,changes_requested,approved,landed,abandoned}; tasks & packages non-empty unique string arrays; last_polled int>=0|null; poll_cadence duration (^[1-9][0-9]*[smhd]$). Invariants: terminal(landed/abandoned)⇒last_polled null; review_units unique; ids unique (ignoring null); null id ⇒ status draft + last_polled null + EXACTLY ONE pending operation type=draft_cr key=`draft-cr:<review_unit>` (crash-safety for CR creation); CR packages resolve in toolchain.packages and kinds match; github CR⇒exactly 1 package, brazil⇒all packages same workspace; and per package the open CRs must form ONE linear branch chain (unique branches, single root whose base∉branches, single successor each, chain end == package.active_branch) (lines 263-295).
elements.porting_note: The branch-chain check (follow_cr_chain, lines 51-62/263-295) is the trickiest invariant: stacked CRs per package form a linked list branch→base ending at active_branch. Port as a graph/linked-list validator. The draft_cr null-id ↔ pending operation coupling is the idempotency handshake for CR creation.

elements.name: open_stops schema + stop KINDS
elements.detail: Lines 306-329, 510-512. Each stop: keys exactly [id,kind,channel,context_ref,authorized_responders,message_id,first_posted,last_polled,last_seen_reply_ts,last_edited,status]; required subset excludes context_ref/last_edited. kind in {publish, confirm_done, ambiguity, stuck, expert_needed, worker_stuck}. status in {awaiting_reply, held}. authorized_responders = unique non-empty strings. (message_id null AND last_seen_reply_ts null) OR both non-empty (a posted Slack thread has both; a file/terminal stop has message_id null). first_posted int>=0. channel MUST reference a configured comms channel. ids unique.
elements.porting_note: These 6 stop kinds are the harness's halt reasons and map to the tier/stop model: publish (external-action approval gate), confirm_done (finish-project decision), ambiguity (manage-confusion), stuck (verify-don't-assume), expert_needed & worker_stuck. Model as `enum StopKind`. 'held' is the [C] hold reply state. authorized_responders gates who may resolve/approve.

elements.name: expert_asks schema (POC DM outreach)
elements.detail: Lines 332-356. keys exactly [id,question,channel,context_ref,policy,poc,dm_channel,thread_ts,asked_at,last_polled,last_seen_reply_ts,status]. status in {awaiting_reply,answered,closed}. policy in {ask_first,search_first,ask_only}. poc = {handle(nonempty), how in {user_named,user_authorized_search,search_found_owner}, source(null|nonempty)}. dm_channel & thread_ts non-empty (the DM lives in its own thread, distinct from open_stops). ids unique.
elements.porting_note: Expert DMs are a separate channel from stops: routed by dm_channel/thread_ts, polled on their own cadence. poc.how is the audit trail required by ask-first policy (principles red flag lines 82-84). Encode poc.how as enum.

elements.name: session / review_state / channel_state / approvals / operations / async_workers schemas
elements.detail: session (359-369): null or {kind:'cron-loop', protocol:'project-manager-heartbeat-v2', engine in {claude-cron,loop}, job_id, cron, registered_at int>=0, cancel_handle} — all non-empty. review_state (370-377): null or {slice_id,signature,attempts int>=1,updated_at} — tracks stuck-retry attempts per slice. channel_state (378-386): [{name,last_posted int|null}], names unique, must reference config channels; post-intake must cover EVERY configured channel exactly (503-509). approvals (387-400): [{id,action,scope,granted_by,granted_at,expires_at?}], ids unique, expires_at>=granted_at. operations (401-420): [{id,type,key,status in {pending,completed,failed},started_at,completed_at?,remote_id?,detail?}], keys unique, completed⇒completed_at set, pending⇒completed_at & remote_id null. async_workers (421-443): [{id,task_id,agent:'codex',tmux_session,workdir,branch,started_at,deadline,last_polled,poll_cadence?,status in {running,orphaned},done_signal,log}], deadline>=started_at, ids unique.
elements.porting_note: operations[] is the idempotency journal for external mutations (post, draft_cr, heartbeat, push, publish, merge…); approvals[] is the grant table. Both are matched by unique key. async_workers model detached codex tmux sessions with a deadline. review_state.attempts is the stuck counter compared against config.stuck_threshold.

elements.name: config.json schema + cross-field rules
elements.detail: Lines 445-498. config keys EXACTLY [comms,cr,heartbeat,stuck_threshold,coordinator_lease_s,multi_agent]. comms={channels(non-empty; each {name,kind in {slack,file,terminal},target(null|nonempty),role in {primary,secondary},update_cadence?,posts?⊆{status,stops,cr_activity,decisions,expert_dm},audience?}; names unique; EXACTLY ONE primary), only_on_material_change(bool), quiet_hours('none'|HH:MM-HH:MM), quiet_hours_tz(tz name regex), stop_backoff, expert_outreach in {ask_first,search_first,ask_only}}. cr MUST equal exactly {"publish_approval":"per_cr"}. heartbeat=duration. stuck_threshold int>=1. coordinator_lease_s int>=60. multi_agent={max_parallel>=1,timeout_s>=1,async_timeout_s>=1}. CROSS-FIELD: coordinator_lease_s >= multi_agent.timeout_s + 60 (line 497). stop_backoff (477-483): non-empty [{until_min(null|int>=0),poll(duration)}] with stop_backoff_ordered = last entry until_min null, exactly one null, until_min values strictly increasing & unique.
elements.porting_note: cr.publish_approval is hard-locked to 'per_cr' — every CR publish needs its own approval; do not make it configurable. stop_backoff is a tiered escalation ladder (poll less often as a stop ages). Enforce the lease>timeout+60 cross-field so a coordinator lease outlives its worker subagents.

elements.name: Autonomy tier / stop model (principles.md + phase headers)
elements.detail: The skill runs at ONE tier: 'max autonomy' (plan.md:8 'the skill runs at max autonomy'; design.md:8). Phase gates are AUTO-WAIVED — proceed through intake→…→done without asking for design/plan approval (plan.md:96 'Do not ask for plan approval'). principles.md:4 'They are not gates and never waive — phase gates are auto-waived, these are not.' principles.md:123-126 pins the stop model: the loop halts ONLY for the subset of principles that halt it — reversibility→irreversible-action HARD stop, verify-don't-assume→stuck stop, manage-confusion-actively→ambiguity stop. External/networked mutations additionally require a matching non-expired approval + a persisted operation intent BEFORE the call (principles.md:49-52).
elements.porting_note: Encode 'tier' as: at max autonomy, phase transitions auto-flow (no human gate) and the ONLY things that stop the loop are (a) the 3 principle-stops, (b) approval gates for external actions (publish/confirm_done), (c) expert_needed/worker_stuck. There is NOT a multi-level tier ladder in these files — do not invent one; the decision is binary per action: does a stop trigger fire → raise open_stops[] + set run.posture=needs_you (only after all independent work exhausted, comms.md:125); else auto-flow.

elements.name: Engineering principles + red flags (continuous, never waive)
elements.detail: principles.md:14-65 lists always-in-force principles each with an excuse/tell: Verify-don't-assume; Surface-assumptions (log to decisions.md before non-trivial work); Scope-discipline; YAGNI; Orthogonality (one branch/CR per plan checkpoint); Manage-confusion-actively (name conflict, post lettered options); Push-back; Reversibility; External-actions-explicit-and-idempotent (approval+operation record); DRY; Chesterton's-Fence; Broken-windows (log to handoff.md); Code-as-liability; Tracer-bullets. Red flags (69-118) are runtime tells to correct NOW: unlogged user corrections need `Source: user — "…"` in decisions.md; a DM without poc.handle+poc.how; retrying a failing fix with no new evidence toward stuck_threshold → route to systematic-debugging; a networked mutation with no matching approval; ledger noise (CURRENT/handoff/progress stale after advance); single-line state.json/config.json (must write via `jq .`).
elements.porting_note: These are prompt/playbook TEXT to BORROW VERBATIM into the worker prompt per phase (they say 'apply in every phase and every dispatched subagent'). The harness does not machine-enforce most of them, but SHOULD enforce the mechanizable red flags: stuck counter vs stuck_threshold, approval-before-mutation, pretty-printed JSON, and 'decisions.md must gain an entry when a fork was resolved'.

elements.name: Comms routing and content classes
elements.detail: comms.md:20-64. Route by content class via config channels[].posts. If posts omitted, PRIMARY channel gets status+stops+cr_activity. Broadcastable classes {status,cr_activity,decisions} go to EVERY channel that accepts them. A `stops` message uses EXACTLY ONE destination (prefer primary if it accepts stops, else first matching in config order) and records destination+message_id in open_stops[]. `expert_dm` goes only to the approved POC. If no channel accepts a class → primary + a sourced decisions.md routing note. Existing conversations don't move when config changes (stop threads keep open_stops[].channel/.message_id; expert DMs keep dm_channel/thread_ts). 5 classes & their send/don't-send rules in the table at 41-47.
elements.porting_note: Borrow the routing table VERBATIM. Encode content class as `enum PostClass {Status,Stops,CrActivity,Decisions,ExpertDm}` and a router that resolves class→channel(s) from config. 'stops = exactly one destination' and 'existing conversations pinned to their original channel' are hard rules.

elements.name: Message format + stop creation/resolution protocol
elements.detail: comms.md:66-158. Blocking ask format: context + question in prose, then each choice on its own line `[A]`/`[B]` + a free-form escape `[C] Something else`; accept letter, free text, or both. Never leave a user-attention request only in internal ledgers — post to stops destination (or primary fallback) AND mirror in CURRENT.md 'Needs you'. Mention (@) a person ONLY when they must act. CREATE a stop (114-127): (1) persist deterministic post operation BEFORE the network call; (2) post once, capture message_id; (3) append full open_stops[] element incl. authorized_responders; (4) name it in CURRENT.md 'Needs you'; (5) ONLY after all independent work exhausted set run.posture=needs_you with this stop id as owner + next pm-due poll epoch. UPDATE: new facts→edit tracked message + update last_edited; same facts→no-op; `[C] hold`→status='held' keep polling; file/terminal→rewrite STATUS.md keep message_id null.
elements.porting_note: The operation-before-post ordering (persist pending post op → post → record thread) closes the crash window and is the idempotency contract — enforce it. Borrow the lettered-options format verbatim into the stop-composition prompt. 'set needs_you only after independent work exhausted' is a scheduler rule the harness owns.

elements.name: Poll replies + authorized-responder gate
elements.detail: comms.md:138-176. Poll ONLY ids in pm-due.sh's due_stops (a CR-check wake does NOT bypass stop backoff). Per due stop: fetch thread; process replies with ts > last_seen_reply_ts oldest-first; compare each reply's AUTHENTICATED sender id against authorized_responders. A reply from anyone else is feedback (log it, advance the reply cursor so it isn't replayed, but keep the stop). Record a sourced decisions.md entry only for a non-trivial ruling; copy binding decisions to handoff.md. Advance last_seen_reply_ts only AFTER the checkpoint is durable; dedupe by (stop id, reply ts). If resolved→remove stop; if unanswered→update only last_polled. An inbound reply via a bound Slack channel is a valid project wake; a direct chat message wakes the project only if it clearly answers a tracked stop or requests continuation (questions leave it parked).
elements.porting_note: Authorization is by authenticated sender id ∈ authorized_responders — the harness must verify identity, not trust content. Reply-cursor (last_seen_reply_ts) advance must be transactional with the durable checkpoint. Dedupe key = (stop_id, reply_ts). This is the human-in-the-loop resolution path.

elements.name: Scheduling/posting gates + quiet hours + Slack fallback
elements.detail: comms.md:177-215. Use pm-due.sh output directly: due_channels, due_stops, due_expert_asks, posting_allowed. Polling is read-only and CONTINUES during quiet hours; only NEW non-urgent posts wait for posting_allowed:true. When comms.only_on_material_change=true, post status only after a real change (task/checkpoint complete, phase/CR change, decision, stop raised, blocking error); when false, post every due cadence. NEVER add a fake progress.md entry when nothing changed. Update channel_state.last_posted only after an actual successful post, then seal a journal checkpoint. Slack-unreachable fallback: non-blocking status→write STATUS.md digest and continue; blocking question→record locally and pause ONLY the affected track (a file write is NOT user consent); record degraded destination in CURRENT.md/progress.md; on recovery post the unposted question once (never duplicate); keep run 'working' if an independent local track is still runnable.
elements.porting_note: pm-due.sh (see next element) is the SOLE cadence authority — the harness must not recompute schedules in prose. Quiet-hours gates posting but not polling. The post→last_posted→journal-seal sequence is the comms half of the idempotency journal. Borrow the fallback rules verbatim.

elements.name: pm-due.sh cadence logic (the scheduler)
elements.detail: pm-due.sh computes due tracks from state+config+injected NOW. due_crs: non-terminal CRs with non-null id, due if last_polled null or elapsed>=poll_cadence (default 20m). due_stops (lines 154-162): elapsed_min=(now-first_posted)/60; select first stop_backoff entry with until_min null or >=elapsed_min → its poll; cadence=max(that, heartbeat floor); due by last_polled. due_expert_asks (163-169): awaiting_reply only; cadence=1h if asked_at<24h ago else 6h. due_async_workers (170-176): running only; cadence=max(poll_cadence default 5m, heartbeat). due_channels (177-188): none if phase==done; else channels accepting status (posts null→role==primary; else posts∋'status') due by update_cadence (default 2h) vs channel_state.last_posted. Output object also has work:(phase!=done), cr_check, comms, posting_allowed. Quiet hours computed in shell (lines 85-122): posting_allowed=false when local time in [start,end) with midnight wraparound, or start==end (always quiet). lib/scheduling.jq defines duration regex, to_secs, stop_backoff_ordered, and heartbeat_to_cron (heartbeat→cron expression for registering the loop).
elements.porting_note: Port pm-due as the harness scheduler: it is the single authority for what to poll each wake. Reimplement to_secs (s/m/h/d), the stop_backoff ladder lookup (first entry whose until_min covers elapsed age; final null = catch-all), the heartbeat floor (max with heartbeat), and quiet-hours wraparound. heartbeat_to_cron is needed if the harness registers a cron loop; not needed if it drives its own timer.

invariants: Only the current unexpired coordinator-lease owner may seal a checkpoint while state.run.active or a lock dir exists (pm-checkpoint 475-489); sealing requires pm-validate to pass first.

A validated ledger, once sealed, cannot be silently mutated: verify recomputes hashes and fails if any durable content (files except state.json, control_state, material_state, journal_guard, journal) differs from the seal.
Poll cursors (timers.work + all last_polled) and comms last_posted are monotonic non-decreasing and never exceed seal/now time; a CR going terminal is the only allowed reset (to null).

External/networked mutations (post, draft_cr, publish, push, merge, heartbeat) MUST have a matching non-expired approval and a persisted pending operation record BEFORE the network call; operations advance only pending→{completed,failed}, failed→{pending(new started_at),completed}.
Every CR with a null id must be a draft with null last_polled and exactly one matching pending draft_cr operation keyed draft-cr:<review_unit>.
Per package, all open (non-terminal) CRs form exactly one linear branch chain (unique branches, single root, single successor each) ending at that package's active_branch.

state.phase is one of the 9 states {intake,research,design,plan,implement,review,cr,confirming,done}; run.posture=done requires phase=done; run.posture=needs_you (while active) requires an open_stops[] entry whose id == run.owner.
config.cr must be exactly {publish_approval: per_cr}; every CR publish requires its own approval — publishing is never auto-approved.
config.coordinator_lease_s >= config.multi_agent.timeout_s + 60, and coordinator_lease_s >= 60.
config.comms.channels has exactly one primary; post-intake, channel_state must cover every configured channel exactly and Slack channels must have non-empty targets.
stop_backoff is a strictly-increasing ladder terminated by exactly one null until_min (catch-all); pm-due is the sole cadence authority and a CR-check wake does not bypass stop backoff.

A `stops` message goes to exactly one destination recorded in open_stops[]; a stop/question is never left only in internal ledgers — it is posted (or STATUS.md fallback) and mirrored in CURRENT.md 'Needs you'.
A stop is resolved/approved only by a reply whose authenticated sender id is in authorized_responders; all other replies are logged feedback and advance the reply cursor but keep the stop open.
Reply cursor (last_seen_reply_ts) and channel_state.last_posted advance only after the corresponding checkpoint is durable; posting then recording is journal-sealed.

Phase gates auto-waive (max autonomy, no design/plan approval prompts); the loop halts only for the three principle-stops (irreversible-action, stuck, ambiguity), approval gates, and expert/worker stops.
state.json and config.json are always pretty-printed (multi-line via jq .) because humans read and git-diff them; they must each be exactly one JSON object.
needs_you is set only after all independent runnable work is exhausted; an independent local track keeps the run 'working' even when another track is blocked (including on Slack failure).
gotchas: The three canonical hashes overlap but differ subtly: control_state=del(.run); material_state also nulls timers.work + 4 poll cursors; journal_guard additionally drops .session, channel_state.last_posted, and heartbeat/post operations. Getting any deletion wrong breaks the material-change vs bookkeeping-only distinction that gates no-change/journal seals.

verify intentionally does NOT compare state.json's raw file hash nor bookkeeping — only the durable subset — because poll cursors legitimately advance between seal and verify. Do not add state.json to the verify file comparison.

material checkpoint requires the 3 narrative files (CURRENT/handoff/progress) to CHANGE but does NOT itself require material_state to change; conversely no-change forbids material_state change and forbids any of the 5 tracked files changing (state.json may still change its cursors).

review_unit key derivation (sorted, %-encoded packages joined with '+', then ':'+slice_id) is duplicated in pm-checkpoint and pm-validate — implement once. @uri encoding of package names matters for uniqueness.

The coordinator lock is an atomic mkdir directory, not a lockfile; stale takeover falls back to the directory mtime when owner.json is unparseable. flock on the project-state dir separately serializes all mutations — two different locking mechanisms with distinct purposes (lease ownership vs transaction serialization).
pm-checkpoint seal calls pm-lock assert-held with PM_COORDINATOR_LOCK_HELD=1 because it already holds the flock; forgetting this reentrancy flag would deadlock on the same FD lock.
Exit codes are semantic: pm-lock/assert-held return 2 for contention/not-owner/expired vs 1 for usage errors; callers branch on these. Preserve them.

journal session transitions require a matching COMPLETED heartbeat operation whose remote_id == session.job_id — the session block and the operations journal are coupled; you cannot register a session without the corresponding heartbeat op.

The failed→pending operation retry path REQUIRES a strictly larger started_at and null completion fields — this is how idempotent retries are distinguished from replays; equal started_at on a retry is rejected.

pm-due applies a heartbeat floor via max(configured_cadence, heartbeat) to stops and async_workers but NOT to CRs (20m default) or channels (2h default) or expert_asks (fixed 1h/6h) — the flooring is selective.
Quiet hours gate only NEW posts; polling (reading threads) continues. start==end quiet_hours means always-quiet (posting never allowed). Wraparound (start>end) is handled explicitly.

async_workers.agent is constrained to only 'codex' (not claude); async workers are detached codex tmux sessions with a deadline and done_signal — the harness dispatches claude/codex as stateless one-shot workers, but the async-worker record models a specifically long-running detached codex run.

principles.md is largely prompt TEXT to borrow verbatim into worker prompts (it explicitly targets 'every dispatched subagent'), but its red flags encode a few machine-enforceable rules (stuck counter vs stuck_threshold via review_state.attempts, approval-before-mutation, pretty-printed JSON) the harness should enforce, not just prompt.

There is no multi-level autonomy tier in these files — the skill is single-tier 'max autonomy'. Do not build a tier ladder; the stop-vs-autoflow decision is per-action (does a stop/approval trigger fire?), driven by the 6 open_stops kinds + approvals table.
